People seem to either hate or love this place so I had to check it out. Me? I fell in love as soon as I went inside and saw that tall red staircase with that beautiful looming chandelier. Yes, perhaps it is a little musty with all that partying history but that is not a reason not to go to The Emerald Supper Club. Rarely will you come across a place that is so retro, so cool.The service was a little cool and so was my food, however. My BBQ Pork Waffle Fry Poutine was barely warm so I had to wolf it down before The Hard Rock Miners Singalong began. I totally loved the goat cheese dip with caramelized onions, super tasty and the homemade potato chips were super crisp. I can see why most people talk about the waffle fries. This place knows how to deep fry.Despite having some issues with the food, the music venue was fantastic (call ahead to make reservations if you want to be sure to see the band) and the setting so much fun. I don't think I have ever been to quite a fantastically retro place before. I loved every second of it and can't wait to go back.For my full review: http://www.suziethefoodie.com/emerald-supper-club/

Well 85°C is finally here in Austin. I've been to many other locations across the country, so like many others, I'm glad its here as it finally shores up something that Austin is desperately missing: asian bakery.The bread selection here feels smaller compared to other ones I've been to, but its no less fresh. I appreciate them putting the calorie count on the breads. Personal favorites include the boroh almond half moon and the taro. As for the drinks, I can't realize advise the tea - it's surprisingly bad that tastes like murky water with equally as bad pearls. I do hear the sea salt coffee is quite delectable though, so stick to their coffee game.They have a decent size dining area and good cakes too, so grab a friend and sit down and chat.

Pizza slices were good size for price. Taste is fine nothing great and not bad. If your nearby and want a slice grab a piece but if you are looking for a great piece of pizza sorry to say, keep looking. Good specials each day so if you want to try this place go for it, it won't break the bank and I feel it is a decent food taste to value. Service was excellent though.

First of all I'd say they are more of a 3.5 star place for me.  We started with an amuse of a lightly smoked salmon crudo and a small butternut squash soup.  I then had foie gras 2 ways (seared and a torchon).  The torchon I think was the better of the 2 preparations although there was a string of connective tissue in it which I found a little unappetizing.  Also I felt that it could have benefited from a couple of crystals of sea salt on the top to give it a little more flavor.  My wife had the organic lettuce salad with fruits and olive oil.  It was well.... a salad nothing bad about it but I would not call it outstanding either.  I had the rack of lamb and my wife had a piece of soy glazed sable fish.  The sable fish had a nice texture.  It was kind of like a cross between cod and sea bass and it had some firmness but not as firm as cod and a slight buttery flavor to it but not as buttery as sea bass either.  I ordered my lamb chops medium rare but they came out a little closer to medium.  For dessert we both had a Grand Marnier souffle.  It's been a VERY long time since I have had a properly done souffle.  They certainly have a good example of the breed here.  Also try the Canadian ice wine here.  It is addictive.  If the torchon and the lamb had been properly executed I'd have given them 4 stars.  At this price point, you have to execute flawlessly with every dish.

Everything about this venue is Perfect! Every inch of the place is gorgeous! There is ivy, cactus, beautiful trees, a pool, a horse and donkey, views of the hill country and on and on! It is perfect Texas hill country setting! The staff are absolutely wonderful!  They made my vision come to life and exceeded my expectations! They kept us calm with the crazy pre-wedding rush. They were SO organized! They made sure my husband and I had a drink at all times, were fed, and had backup food/cake in our room. We booked the venue dj and bartenders, which was very convenient.  They too exceeded our expectations!  The venue has a huge beautiful lodge on-site for 15 to stay with a private lodge for bride and groom.  I recommend you do stay the night with the bridal party!! The stars come out so bright and there is a pool/hot tub to relax in after all the craziness of the wedding.  If you are looking for a venue, look no more! This place cannot be topped!!
Great food and excellent service! Prices are fair and steaks are amazing!! My daughter loves the peanuts!

I stopped in here a few weeks ago for some organic potting mix. I found what I needed, and the prices were reasonable. The person who helped me was helpful and friendly, didn't get his name. So I'm new to this gardening thing, and he gave me a few pointers for growing tomato plants. I even got a free cucumber plant. Thanks! The parking lot in the back is a plus too.
Delicious - two of us split the vegie platter (vegan) and there was more than enough food.  Simple interior + nice people.  We will definitely return!

Got out of work early to get nails done. Read reviews for this place and thought I'd give it a try. Perhaps if I got a female tech to do my nails, I'd be happier than I am right now. The male tech was clearly new. Put FOUR coats of polish on my nails plus base and top coat. Needless to say my nails took ages to dry and had air bubbles and streaks through them like prunes. I asked if I could get less polish for a nail that was completely botched and was ignored by himself and his coworker. Frankly, this was an excellent massage.  The location is totally weird and the building is pretty industrial from the outside.  I have to admit, I was nervous to go in- It is so off the beaten path.  However, I just went with it.  This place is nothing fancy but the woman who gave me the massage was thorough and very nice.  I have had terrible insomnia and I expect to sleep really well tonight.  I will definitely go back.
I have dreams about going here.Fast and friendly and the ramen is so yummy!Not as authentic as I would like, but still wicked yummy.No egg in the ramen :(

The real deal. Silvanos is hands-down one of the best Italian restaurants I have ever been to. Nestled in a strip mall between an Indian place and Wing House in Altamonte, it is easy to miss, but trust me this is one you need to go and find. We have been going for a few years now and Silvano (yes, the owner is an adorable Italian chef named Silvano) never disappoints. It is a small, intimate, place that really makes you feel at home. The food does the same; they have all your favorites, plus a few extras that will blow your mind. Great date place, you've gotta try it!

Locally sourced wild game hamburgers that are ridiculously good. The elk burger comes with caramelized onions, butter lettuce and cherry demi-glaze. The bison burger was definitely my favorite with feta cheese, bacon and spinach. The patty had a nice zing to it without being too spicy.

I highly recommend Dr. Davis.  Excellent all around care and a staff that make you feel welcome and relaxed whether you are just coming in for a cleaning or something a bit scarier :-).  I had a recent dental emergency and he was very attentive and understanding and did everything in his power to ensure I received treatment as soon as possible.  You won't regret making the switch to Dr. Davis.
Great food, good prices, wonderful atmosphere! I highly recommend this place. Compared to the restaurants around it, it's one of the best!
Oh, the Atomic Cafe. Home to funky art students, cute boys with glasses, french sodas, memories of acoustic folk/rock/funk shows and fine retro decor. It's a fun place to stop by if you're in Bev'ly.

Friendly and fast service. Mel was awesome! Facility was very clean and new as well! This place is also super easy to get to right on Manchaca which is good to know there is something so close by in case of emergencies.

My friends and I ordered burritos, I love the white card system, but whoever made our food got our orders all mixed up. We figured, whatever, we're hungry -- burritos don't have to be perfect to still be great. But when we bit into them they were COLD, and the service was really fast, which means their ingredients are just hanging around in the kitchen at room temperature. GROSS. My friends wanted to send them back but we figured they would just microwave them or something. I feel lucky we did not get food poisoning from this place. BEWARE!

My baby-daddy and I happened to be in the neighbourhood after unnecessarily being stuck at the Doctor's office for over 2 hours, so we were grumpy and very hungry.It was still early and we were seriously craving a decent breakfast. We walked in and didn't think too much of the place, it's a simple cafe. A few locals were sitting around conversating and there were quite a few seniors reading their papers and eating their breakfasts. The service was really nice.We ordered a Large Basic Breakfast that came with Pancakes and we also ordered the Hash. The breakfasts were good, but the Pancakes, OMG the PANCAKES were FAB! What was a grumpy morning was suddenly filled with rainbows and leprechauns. My frown was turned upside down, a life milestone accomplished - find the unicorn of pancakes for breakfast and find them we finally did! It was that much more special too because I wasn't expecting it.Did I mention they have mother-effingly-good pancakes here? Yum yum yum.

I had the spinach quiche, and it was just - ok. I have low expectations for their other menu items, so I probably won't be back again unless I'm just coming for a cookie or muffin. It was pretty cheap, but not priced cheap enough for the quality of food in my opinion. Tables and chairs are old and rickety, but it seemed clean enough. Woman who helped me at the counter was very pleasant!

Hmmmmmmmmmmmm! I second, third,fouth and fifth about all the wonderful things that have been said about this place pertaining to their food and the customer service. On my new found journey as a vegetarian, this resturant came right on time! Not only was the food great, I've met wonderful people while there; kindred spirits! On to the food, I have had the jackfruit philly, mock salmon burger and the buffalo fried cauliflour. Can we say delicious! I would have to say the that mock salmon is my favorite! I've been twice this month. During my first visit, I called to find out what time they closed and was informed 9pm and I called at 8:40pm. I was encouraged to come in and upon my arrival, I was asked if I was the one that called. My bf was not into trying this spot and stated that he would get something else but thank goodness he tried it. This is how I discovered that I would have the mock salmon on my next visit. You ever pay for something and wasn't quite satisfied or that it did not deserve your money, you won't get that here! Both times I ate in, which may make some people feel uneasy due to the location. I was a bit put off by the location but I am so glad that I did try it! As good as the food is, I hope that they are not only able to keep that location but branch out as well. The cook has come out to make sure that I enjoy my food and I appreciate that. The food is cooked to order so be patient, it's worth it!

Pretty good value-- $5.99 including tax for a chicken shawarma but not a fabulous product.The ingredients were fine and the chicken was very delicious, but the shawarma itself was made out of only a single pita, it wasn't grilled, and the layering of veggies/chicken/sauce left for a lop-sided eating experience.All in all, I'd go back, but only if I were really craving it.

Yes. Yes. Yes.Fried chicken with mac and cheese and onion rings. A whisky drink (longwell) and and a salted caramel cheesecake that magically separates all of the flavors and punches you with the saltiness at the end (yum).Portions are GENEROUS. Enough for two in one entree, easily. The staff were super nice, quick, and attentive. I'm sad that I will only get here once before the move to Cali.

It's Ok. I very much want to see these guys do well. We REALLY need Chinese delivery in our little neck of the woods. I just wasn't floored by the entree's. What I will go back for are the egg rolls and dumplings. I hope they broaden the menu somewhat. I had the Mongolian beef. They do a nice treatment with large pieces of steak. The General Tas'o Chicken was just not my favorite. You can tell they are really trying to elevate the normal family Chinese Food experience. The flavors just didn't hit for me personally. Admittedly, the entree's may be more authentic than what a guy like from Atlanta might realize. I will put in a plug for the ice-cream side of the house. The kids love it and ask to go back.

The restaurant ambiance was great and the service was wonderful.  I had the pecan chicken and it was one of the better chicken dish's I have had.  We ate early but had a reservation and were seated right away.  The staff remembered our name throughout the process as well and even the valet parking attendant's were extra friendly.  Though the food is a little pricey the taste and the atmosphere convinced us that this has to go on our short list of great places around Atlanta.
It's called FD's Grill now, but same menu and delicious margaritas. Great food and great prices. Nothing mind blowing... Just good food and drink at reasonable prices. I'm a fan and so's the wifey.

This is a beautiful hotel right in the heart of the very busy Orlando International Airport. This is not a cheap or budget friendly hotel by any means but it is very nice. I don't feel that you get as much for the money as you should however, that's just me. The staff are beyond helpful and friendly. The location is convenient and this is where Disney does their transportation service to and from Port Canaveral for their cruise line which is the only reason in choosing this location but we would stay here again. Everything was clean in the hotel and they have a nice pool on the roof of level 6, but no hot tub. The fitness area is adequate. We did not have a tv built into the mirror of our bathroom most reviews have mentioned but it was a handicap room.

Second time hitting up Dragon Ball Tea House and it's just as good as I remember! My buddy and I dropped by after our sushi dinner for some late night BBT. The place was still relatively busy, especially for a Sunday evening. I guess everything is just busier in Vancouver. MUST move here soon, someone adopt me.We each got our own BBT. Man oh man, there are way too many flavours to choose from.- Pudding flavour ($4.50 + $0.50 for grass jelly) - under their special drinks menu, I've never tried a full on pudding BBT. I gave it a shot and it was tasty but definitely caters to someone with a sweet tooth. A whole drink itself is overkill but I powered through.Persimmon ($4.50 + $0.50 for pearls) - this is one of their fresh flavour drinks. Always go with fresh! My buddy thoroughly enjoyed it and I had a sip as well, it was fresh and tasted just like persimmon.Dragon Ball Tea House is awesome! One of my favourite spots in Van to get BBT. Definitely worth the trip out to get your fix. Now I want one right now.

I loved the food but the guy at the food cart was extremely rude. He also said I would have to pay extra (it's not written anywhere about this extra charge so I think he just made it up) if I didn't eat at the bar even though it's a food cart. He said I would have a 20 min. wait so I would have to move my car as I parked in a 15 min. spot and I asked for a number and he made it seem like I was an idiot for asking for an order number. So I said forget it...I probably won't return just because of him though the lady, who showed up after I re-parked, was quite cordial.Two stars because the food is decent (fries were burnt).

Should have read the reviews....The staff was pretty dull. Not rude, but not engaged either. The bagel was 'aight. I asked for it toasted and received a slightly warm doughy bagel. The bacon scallion cream cheese had a lot of rubbery bacon fat in it. Gross. Oh, and it was something like $5.50 after tax for my bagel in cream cheese. Maybe if that was the best bagel and cream cheese I've ever had, but this certainly was not the case.

Amazing Colombian tapas in Ohio!? Check. This place was delicioius. The service was fast and great, and the food prices were extremely fair as well. Can't wait to come back here next time I'm passing through Ohio.

It is quite impressive that this place has a business selling basically one item.  But hey, they do a good job at it and when you think about it, there are quite a few possible permutations of ingredients that can make up a bowl.  Anyways, I was a happy customer since I got the order like I wanted and got it quick.

We had 4 dishes a few months back, all were so bad I can't even explain. Fried potstickers were mushy not crunchy, the soup had mystery meat in it that very tasted off. This is not one of those dives with great cheap food, it's just a dive.Chrismas decor all year round lol. There was so much noise from the lottery machine, the tv, the radio. The most noise came from what I believe was the owners kids, they were eating at another table and each kid had their own noisy video game to play. It's not a bistro, but they call themselves that. All the good Asian restaurants are on NE 82nd. Nothing fancy there either, but delicious food.The only reason I don't give them 1 star is because no one was mean to me. It's like your typical Asian restaurant, not super friendly but not rude. My friend left as much food behind as I did. Oh yeah, and they were 8 points from failing their health inspection report earlier this year :/ Wish I had checked that first:http://www.co.washington.or.us/HHS/EnvironmentalHealth/FoodSafety/restaurant-inspections.cfm

Mmmmmmm, Athenian Chicken Salad! It's the best, but I get it with the gyro meat instead of chicken and ask for the dressing and other sauce on the side (they drown it if you don't). Athenian Grill is one of my favorite lunch spots. It's pretty quick as it's a walk up counter, but get there early. Today the line was almost out the door. Seating is usually not a problem but every now and again, you get tool boxes who sit and linger even though the line is out the door and people are standing there, looking helpless as they look around for a place to sit.To those jerks who sit there, discussing the selling price of Dell today, I say, get your ass up fools. Sometimes the busboys will come by and bus their tables, asking if they're done, giving them a hint, and these jacktards still sit, oblivious that there are people besides them.The baklava is beautiful at Athenian. It's really big and chock full o' nuts, as well as topped with a slice of preserved lemon. If you can stomach it (the portions here are huge), I highly suggest it.

Had my birthday dinner here with some family out on the outdoor patio which was the perfect setting. I tried the Frosé very refreshing and sweet, I will definitely be ordering it again. For my meal I ordered one of the new summer items, the Clam Shrimp & Chivalini Sausage Linguine, very tasty!

I seriously cannot find another Moroccan restaurant in Boston that is as authentic and consistent as Moroccan Hospitality. They used to be in Malden, now in Somerville, and the food is still consistently good. Their food made me feel like at home: nothing fancy or conceptual; just the most true and honest home cooking delivered to your table. Tonight I just had the Lamb couscous, and Moroccan mint tea. I know I will get their Tagine next time I am there. Hope more people will know and actually come to this place to try their food.

My 3 stars are for the Candler Park joint only as the others I go to (Peachtree, Howell Mill, Ponce) have all been good to me and I would easily give those ones 5 stars...this one not so...Candler Park Fellinis WAS my favorite of all the other Fellinis, mostly because of the location and nice patio, but the last time I went I wasnt so impressed, due to the fact how pathetic the pizza I ordered was when it came to my table, it was easily my worst experience I've had when eating here, I only order 3 toppings, the slice comes to about $4, that I'm not bothered about, it was the way they pathetically sprinkled the most smallest amount of feta cheese I have ever seen, it was a little 1 inch line up the middle of the slice, and the onion...I could have counted the bits of onion on one hand, yeah, about 5 bits of onion, it was weak. My family are visiting from the UK in July and I was planning on taking them to the Candler Park location as its so nice in the summer, but now I'm really considering taking them to the Buckhead, Peachtree location instead as I would be too embarrassed if they were to serve us that half arsed weak attempt at a pizza they did when I went there last. So that is the reason I removed 1 star, the reason I took away a second star is because of the state of the patio when I visited last, there was shit everywhere, the tables had crap all under them like they didnt know how to sweep up or something and there was bits of pizza stuck to the table leg, and there was a fuck off cockroach harassing me and my friends for a cigarette, he was obviously there for the scraps of food lying around the place and the fact the patio wasnt regularly cleaned was obviously what attracted his kind there. This particular Fellinis has gone drastically down hill and theres a good chance I wont be going back to this one, and thats a shame cause I liked this one.

The green beans mixed with spaetzle and bacon may be one of the best side dishes ever devised. The Reuben made w a big pink slab o' sausage was just OK. Good service and tasty beer. Worth another visit next time I'm in Columbus.

I've long been on record as having been such the fan of BBQ that short of a proprietor up and taking a swing at me, chances are I'm bound to appreciate it. And though I couldn't help but chuckle at how different this place might be if it were, say, R. Kelly's BBQ (those jokes go off the rails in a hurry), when I stopped in for lunch yesterday and had my way with a chopped BBQ sandwich (and some chips, natch), I couldn't have been happier. One thing that hits you when you're in here is that the place is *clean*, I mean particularly clean in this era of hole in the wall BBQ joints where the smoke has long since settled into the wood. So the clean may not be for everyone, but I in particular appreciated it. Lunch was plenty affordable and didn't take long to happen, and as I'm by here pretty often, I'm sure I'll be back again. Hey, ya gotta, eat, right?

Love this place!! First of all, the service is really great.  They guide you through the line of ingredients which is all fresh and all the sauces are made in house. First you choose the from the wraps or a bowl, rice, and then the meat (you can mix and match). There is a wide variety of veggies, toppings, and sauces to add to your wrap.  The salmon I got melted in my mouth and the sweet and tangy sauce I got on top was the perfect flavor to bring everything together.  I'm happy I found a place that satisfies my sushi cravings for a reasonable cost and doesn't leave me starving shortly after.

this place is definitely better than fire on the mountain...i am ohioan, pennsylvanian, arizonian and oregonian..and bdubs has always been good...except the hillsboro bdubs which actually sucks and needs to shut down...beaverton is great too but tualatin is absolutely the best...almost as great as the one in akron oh...:)you can order splits or drums separate, wet, dry or normal dosage of sauces ...plenty of flavors...carribean jerk is my favorite...slow heat...:)

I bought a LivingSocial deal to this place a few weeks ago, so my boyfriend and I went last night and it was AWESOME!We got the Backyard BBQ pizza, a chicken quesdilla and two Shipyard Pumpkin Ales= die of yumminess! And although our eyes were waaaaaay bigger than our stomachs, now we have some awesome leftovers for the Pats game today!Will definitely be coming back!
I would give them 10 stars if I could. Had windows tinted on a new car. Fastest service I've experienced from such a vendor. Also, BEST customer service.
Svetlana was great! We hired her for a resident event to draw caricatures of resident pets. It was a huge hit and our residents loved it! Would definitely hire her again.
Amazing place, with a beautiful and big patio! waiting for italian food - from Patrizi's

Monday night I attended the first Friends and Family dinner at Flip.My  first impression was how friendly the staff was. Had a glass of wine at the bar were the bartenders enthusiastically shared their excitement about the menu with suggestions of their favorites. Upon being seated our server immediately greeted us with a casual professionalism.My group made several selections from this very unique take on the traditional burger. I found several selections I liked and a few misses. The pate burger was my favorite. The veggie burger my least favorite. Loved the vodka batter onion rings and the hand cut french fries. Not so crazy about the vegetable of the day which was a unique take on cauliflower though others at my table loved it. Overall I think Richard and his partners have a winning concept here. As the interior was not yet  completed I am eager to go back and see the finished look. If the spot-on service, knowledgeable staff, and consistency of product remain this restaurant will become an Atlanta favorite.
I like to tasty wok good salt paper ribs &  GT shrimp n seafood panda five noodles everything so good

I haven't been in a while but for a minute there I was getting an order to go for about 3-4 weeks straight--and I don't do that at any one spot in particular.  You can't miss this place, they have red, blue and white umbrellas and tables just outside the entrance.  The food is SOOOO good, my favorite is pork anything from this establishment!  Every time I went, it was always packed, and it is a very small space.  They only have one server and she's running that place; and they have a young person running the register.  I always get my food to go and the wait for it is probably 10-15 minutes.  I've tried almost all they appetizers and they were all yummy and l like I said, I do mostly pork entrees because you just can't go wrong with pork!  You can park on the street or there is a private lot just down the block headed south on the same side of the street as the restaurant.

On snow  days this Starbucks is a gathering place of locals. I miss the comfy overstuffed chairs,But now I see that when it's packed with parents and snow  boarding kids, with a line out the door  the tall tables work fabulously.How in the heck did my Barista remember my name in this crowd? I gotta give them credit for making the effort to know us locals.

I'm so sad the old chef left. When we first started to come here - it was SO delicious and the menu seemed to change frequently (which I like). The mussels with julienned veggies and garlic toast was to die for, but alas - it is no more.We have gone back maybe 3 times since the (original or at least last chef) left and all 3 times it's just been ok - pretty boring forgetttable meals. The menu has been the exact same (except specials) all 3 times over a 10 month period and nothing really stands out that much. The mac and cheese - meh I can make it better at home. The steak - I've had better at so many places. the braised short ribs - I've had SO much better elsewhere. It just felt like the quality of food went downhill and so did the flavor (it was bland). I do have to say the drinks are fun and tasty (lots of specialty martinis) and a decent wine list. Also the servers have always been friendly, but occasionally on the slow side to bring dishes/refills.

Best experience we had in Boston. We were here for 2 days of our New England vacation and packed in as much of Boston as we could. We were set on doing the Sam Adams Brewery but almost went to Harpoon at the last minute due to a few bad reviews - so glad we didn't!! Brewery was a LOT easier to get to than they made it seem and the experience was too notch

I was very impressed with the quality of the buffet food. You know with a buffet, it is usually hit or miss. But, wow. I was very impressed with the quality of the food and the authenticity of the place. And the cream puffs were to die for.

I've been here twice for dress alterations. The first time, I showed up a few hours after my dress was scheduled to be ready. She needed another hour, so I just had to shop around and then went back and got it. The second time was a nightmare. As I was getting fitted, two customers came in for their items and were told that they weren't ready yet. So when I was told my dress would be ready in a week, on Monday, I assumed it would be later than that. So I went in on Thursday and it still wasn't ready. I was told to come back on Monday. I went later that week...still not ready. So finally on my third attempt, after three weeks instead of one, the dress was ready.It's clear the woman working here is just two busy. But I would have rather been told it would take three weeks from the start, instead of having to come in three times. And a phone call explaining that the item is not ready would have been great, but that didn't happen.

I have been here once before and actually really enjoyed the food.  The mac & cheese is delish and the french fries are tossed in truffle oil--a nice touch..However, last night, I was treated so rudely by the manager I will never come back--and this is to their detriment since I live just blocks from the new location in Charlestown I was hoping to visit for brunch soon.We walked in to find the place jammed, and we were only wanting a seat at the bar.  The hostess sent us upstairs to the bar on the 3rd level, where they said two seats had just opened up from people they had just seated.  Up we went, to find two people who were seated at a table moving to the openings at the bar, and they offered us their table.  We made our move to sit at the table when the manager, who saw it all go down, rudely told us to get away from the table because he had a waiting list.  All we wanted was a drink at the bar...but hey my money's as green as anybody else's.  I'll just spend it elsewhere.
I go here every time I'm in Boston! Try the lychee boba milk tea with extra lychee jelly :-)
Service was great, portions were perfect for the pricing. Three co-workers ordered the salmon on a plank and loved it.

I was a there for a professional conference. spacious is an understatement. rivaling large hotels in atlanta, this nice hotel is a premier  place for business and social events. of course aquatic themes abound but nothing seems in excess and there is a unique chess sets for public use in the expansive lobby. Staff is confident, but parking is insanely expensive.  an assortment of food spots line International going towards Universal Studios. I found a sushi spot within a mile that was excellent. Perhaps i will yelp it?!  The lobby is also accented with comfortable bungalow seating indoors. The continental breakfast was good for continental - the fruit was sweet and crisp.Starbucks on the ground level gives this hotel a community feel and caters to hotel patron's caffeine jones. Enjoy Orlando!

I love Jeremiah's Italian Ice.  The service is always great and staff is always smiling and always willing to let you sample any flavor without sensing it as a disruption.  I got the Orange Smash, I think it was called and it was awesome.  Their ice cream alone is so creamy and rich and tasty.  Man, just the ice cream is great...add the Italian ice to it and it is magic!  When near a Jeremiah's Ice, you have to stop
Food was fresh and delicious. Very reasonable prices. Will definitely take my family to eat there again soon!
Started this review months ago and never finished. Awesome place! Do not pass up an opportunity to get a sammich here!

Great Store.......BUT, if you don't shop there for 6 months, all your loyalty points get nuked....a pretty RAW deal.  For an added bonus...no empathy whatsoever from the management there.....I'll stick with Liquor Mart....

I'm with other reviewers who were underwhelmed.  Portland has some viscious competition for breakfast places but even so...the good experience here ended with being seated quickly (early on a Sunday).Decor - I can get past less than chic surroundings when all else is worthy.  In this case it just gave us flaws to look at while waiting.Service - bad is really all you can say.  Impolite to rude.  Orders were incorrect.  Generally it didn't seem if anyone cared if we were happy or not.Food - over-priced and underwhelming.  Everything was very basic and portions were small.  I prefer a portion like this to the 2000 cal meal you are presented other places, but not when I'm paying over $10 for a plate with no meat or seafood on it.  Like another reviewer, we were also given one sliced strawberry (in October) as the fruit with the meal.We live in a beautiful city with a great food culture.  No need to come here with so many other places to choose from!

This place is super cool. It's like a sports bar feel but fance and I dig that. Andrea was our server tonight and she was super sweet and the perfect server. They don't have that many vegetarian options, but we had the chips and queso--was delicious! The house salads were huge but fresh and tasty! I def recommend coming here for a date night. The frozè wasn't very good but they have a good wine / cocktail selection. The place is candle lit and trendy. Into it! Cool trendy east side place for sure!

Across the street but forever in my heart. Love the coffee and super sweet and helpful staff here. Whole mexican beans are my treat to me and I'll also indulge in a house made cup from time to time. Very much a neighborhood intergenerational place to hang that feels welcoming.

I brought my new rescue dog in to get spayed by Dr. Matagrano this week and was very impressed. She was very kind, funny, and thorough. She took the time to do a full exam on my dog and found problems like a skin infection that the prior vet completely missed. The poor puppy had been scratching like crazy and thanks to Dr. Matagrano, she is finally on the mend! The doctor suggested we postpone her spay until her skin infection had time to heal, which I found thoughtful and wise. I will definitely be returning to her and would highly recommend her to anyone who is looking for a caring, intelligent vet!

I've had several hairstylist here cut my hair - every time it's been really good. However it seems that There is a lot of turnover. The one person that I've consistently gone to is Lana, I think she's the manager, and she's really good. Reasonably priced similar but better than a Supercuts or that kind of chain. Open seven days

Meh. That about sums up my visit to this place. The food, ok. I ate there last night and don't even remember what I had. Sad. I will say that the staff was very friendly and attentive. The big issue is that management insists on stuffing this place full of tables, likely to break even with the ridiculous rent they are paying, thanks Obama. I didn't really appreciate hearing about the couple next to me chat about their cats digestive problems while at dinner. Anyway, I recommend passing this place as an option, unless of course you're interested in hearing what Nancy from the North Shore wants to do with her life (pssst she wants to meet a nice guy who doesn't play games). Don't we all, Nancy, don't we all.

My husband and I were visiting Portland and looked on Yelp for a good breakfast place. This one had good reviews so we gave it a shot. We made a decision that we were 100% satisfied with.We had the Sugar Waffle with seasonal fruit and the Blueberry pancakes. They were delicious, as is the peppered bacon as well as the homemade ketchup. Amazing. Try it.

I was so impressed with Othello from Superior Shuttle.  Not only did he text me before I even departed my flight, but he walked me through exiting the airport and finding his van.  He was talkative and professional - if using Superior Shuttle in Atlanta, ask for Othello!

Oh heck freaking YES!Had their Tuesday special which was a marinated chicken breast, eve, beans and corn tortillas.  I tore into it not because I was hungry but because it was delicious af! Typically the rice at places is bland. Not here! Sooo good! The rice was the first to go followed by the beans. Those beans were spot on. The chicken breast was lean, flavorful and tender! Not something I get at all Mexican cuisine spots.  Seems like they make their own tortillas and boy were they warm and delicious! Got it to go and still the service was great as well as my meal was warm upon opening at home. I cannot wait to try more menu items!!

I have been a customer for almost 30 years, when I had them check out a used 320 I was interested in.  Ended up buying a new one, and dealt with the dealership during the warranty period.  Looked up Mike when the warranty expired, though, and have been going there ever since.  Working on only BMWs is important to me, but the thing that is particularly impressive is that not only has Mike been there all these years, but Craig has as well.  both are extremely knowledgeable, honest, and just plain nice to work with.  Jeff D

Excellent rostessterie chicken is the staple here and it shows. The chicken was cooked perfectly with a slight charred skin that was packed with flavor. The 1/2 chicken order with yucca, beans and rice was plenty of food for someone to feast and take home for later. Very good restaurant located just outside Windermere in McGuire Publix shopping center. Enjoyed the food and look forward to eating here again. The jalapeño sauce is the shit.

Ice cold beer, great margaritas and rum punches (lots of varieties of flavors) super cheap! Dive-ish atmosphere, right in Quincy Market area. Great food! Had a grilled cheese with brisket on it that was out of this world. Came with 6 people. Not a traditional bar menu, but worth the risk. Everything we had was very good. Mussels appetizer, wings. Quesadillas, grilled cheese, fries uniquely seasoned. All very tasty and fresh. If you are looking for a good place for a quick bite and cold drinks, take a chance on Sissy K's
Great place and atmosphere. Food was fantastic, service was excellent. Would highly recommend.
Service was ok. Amount of meat on my roast beef sandwich was very weak. Cool building though.

I have heard so many people rave about their addiction to Chipotle since I arrived in Atlanta. Never had a desire to try it, but figured I check out what the hype was all about since I was hungry and it was close to where I was. I ordered a steak burrito with white rice and had them add some guacamole. It was a good size and hit the spot, but I can't say that I understand what the hype is all about other than it being fast if your looking to grab something better than the typical fast food on your lunch hour. Being from SoCal, I haven't found any Mexican food in the south that satisfies, but if I'm going to eat fast food-type Mexican, I'd rather go to Mo's where I can get chips for free and a choice of different salsas. No complaints, but I don't see myself running back to have it again anytime soon.

As we inch ever closer to full-blown summer in the city, Earnest Ice Cream's relatively newish brick and mortar scoop is getting in full swing with line ups out the doors for cones and cups of their addictive artisanal ice cream.At the shop, I opted for a double scoop of 33 Acres of Malt and mint chip in a cup (for easier handling and fear of melting). The malt was absolutely delicious in its texture and intense malty essence just as the mint was light and crisp in its understated flavouring.I'm also a fan of the trio of standard favourites: whiskey hazelnut, salted caramel, and milk chocolate flavours. Each bring their own unique set of taste and flavours made with local ingredients wherever possible.I grabbed a jar of Matchstick espresso flake to takeaway. It was rich and full of refreshing coffee flavour.With the sun and summer just around the corner, Earnest is shaping up to continue its must stop  status as a destination for ice cream lovers to cool off for the refreshment.
I love love love calamari and pad thai and basil pad thai, red curry as well. The host is very nice and welcome. I love dine in as well as order togo tons of time. Recommend!

Why why WHY must their parking be terminally stuck in SUCK?Alas, you can't order anything in Alon's and go wrong, but I'll only visit if: a) I'm already in the area b) parked elsewhere (legitimately) and c) someone else goads me into it.

I'm very particular about my tuna fish subs. For a food that is so simple to make that even a child could do it, one still has to realize that there is a particular taste for every individual.Mayo or Miracle Whip? What is the tuna to dressing ratio? Celery or no celery? Onions? Canned in water or oil?Tuna may be the most simple yet most complicated sandwich one could eat. And I think Harry O's did a good job and met my requirements of what a good tuna creation is.But Harry lost points elsewhere. I asked for lettuce, tomatoes, and pickles...I think there were roughly 3 or 4 pickle slices on my sub. Tomatoes totaled the same. Yet the lettuce overflowed out of the top of the sub and dropped all over my plate, my floor, and my lap. It was a mess of lettuce.The sub roll was nothing unique - definitely not baked fresh as it looked and tasted store bought. Some places can pull off using store bought bread, but they usually compensate with the other ingredients, or as I like to say, the ESSENCE of a sandwich. The service was nothing friendly. Kind of cold and strictly business. I felt nothing personal about this establishment which is usually one of the best things about buying from small business.In the end, two stars for very low/fair prices for the neighborhood as well as a successful tuna fish concoction. Go here for cheap food if that's what you're looking for. Me? I'll be at one of the other bazillion restaurants in the neighborhood.
The environment was so friendly, you can chat with strangers in the same booth. I ordered hazelnut coffee, it was so goooood！!

Horrible experience.  We have eaten here before.  On this visit, we had a reservation and were promptly seated.  Our waiter was at the table just after we sat down.  He took our drink order and salad order.  When he returned with our drinks we placed our dinner order that consisted of three side dishes.  Fettuccine Alfredo, spaghetti marinara, and spicy sausage.  What seemed to be longer than expected for our order, our waiter brought the fettuccine alfredo and spaghetti marinara.  He immediately left.  Both of these dishes were lukewarm at best.  The spicy sausage never came nor did the waiter come back by the table to check on us or offer a drink refill.  After about 15 minutes I got  his attention and asked about the sausage, his reply was that it should be coming.  After at least another 10 minutes he brought it and dropped it quickly on the table with no comment and left.  No management was ever seen.  Finally got the waiter's attention again, sent the sausage back and asked for our check.  That took time also.  Just the worst in service, lukewarm food, and no concern apparently by management to check on the customers.  Too many choices in the Arena District for this place to expect us to return.

We got lots of carbs: Mentaiko (Chewy pasta with cod roe on menu) 4/5: SO GOOD-Perfect balance of butter, umami, and spicy on the al dente pasta (tastes like decent pasta), with a little seaweed topping. I was the only one at our table that liked/loved it because I love creamy pasta, and they don't like butter, so if you like buttery, rich pastas, get this! The sauce is a little bit chunky/grainy and it would nice nice if there's a bit more seaweed to flavor and not just garnish, but otherwise absolutely delicious.Okonomayaki 3/5: Delicious, generous size portioned, but sauce a bit too thick on top and I couldn't taste any shrimp or pork as advertised on the menu. The dough texture was kind of sticky and mushy--Not sure if it's supposed to be like that but I didn't like that aspect. It was fine and I could see it being a filling but small carb-loaded meal for one, but didn't live up to all the expectations I had after watching skilled chefs make it on TV. If you haven't had it before, skip it here and try it somewhere else, I will too!Omusoba 3/5: Perfectly fried and seasoned egg blanket, but the noodles inside taste like greasy Chinese takeout, and ruined the crispy egg exterior. Good overall, but not great.Sashimi Carpaccio 2/5: 6-7 slivers of sashimi on a bed of shaved radish and garnished with micro kale. Looks cute and fancy but no, a scam for $9.95, and didn't taste super fresh.Riceless sushi roll thing (forgot the name but picture attached) 3/5: Medley of little bits of raw fish (sashimi scraps hello) and some cucumber, on top of a bed of radish. Interesting and my first time having raw fish rolls without rice-pretty good flavor, but nothing mind blowing. I honestly really like the shaved radish. We really wanted to get the Kobore for some fresh uni and a DEAL but they said they ran out and would substitute uni with eel and we were like never mind. Bummer. My friends had a ramen which I didn't touch and it was cheap at $8 for a pretty big bowl and they said comparable to Santouka and stuff around Boston.Ambiance: Not really that well maintained in terms of cleanliness, which is concerning given that this place serves raw fish. I get that real Izakayas aren't sparkling clean, but I'm still concerned. Other comments: Valet parking for $5 on a pouring, raining day was so worth. The guy that takes phone calls ( I think he's the owner?) is pretty cool and trendy ( in Puma sneakers lol), and friendly with the customers, but is a bit slow when you make reservation/confirm details probably because the restaurant is so just make sure to confirm your reservation details. Overall verdict: Uncertain-I don't think there's anything like this around here and the food was pretty good, but I'm just concerned about freshness here. I'll come back to try the Kobore sushi (and make sure when I make reservation they will have it LOL) and if it turns out unfresh I'll probably just keep coming back to try the cooked foods.

Smash Putt is is so intrinsically Portland! How did we not already have this? And it's only here for a limited time? WHAT?! BAR THE EXISTS! CHAIN YOURSELF TO THE EXTERIOR! From the outside it doesn't look like much - but don't let that stop you. Solider on into the abandoned looking building that once held Hung Far Low and enter the world of Smash Putt. If you think you know your way around the Mini Golf rodeo - think again. This takes Mini Golf, blind folds it, spins in around, and drops it into a whole new world. You'll crawl under lasers, they'll drill a hole in your ball, you'll sabotage your opponents, you'll scratch and sniff your way to a par 3, and you're still not done yet. Smash Putt is the brain child of artists. Each hole holds it's own unique bag of tricks to keep you on your toes. I came on a Saturday night and while busy it wasn't overwhelming - although I could see how it could get that way. If you're a stickler for order,  just cool your heals, and enjoy the craziness that is Smash Putt. There is no order or rhyme of reason to the holes, it' just for fun. Better still - they have a full bar! I had a fantastic time - there is really nothing like this and for $11 dollars I think it is, it's well worth your time.

As I have had the pleasure of meeting, and working with,  many of the very qualified and competent staff I have also encouraged many other people to go here for a variety of services.  Every single one has thanked me profusely.  Im a health care professional, NP,  and recognise the professional approach to be of the highest level. The skill level of the staff is stellar. I've been coming here for years and plan to continue!
Good food and cold beer with a great selection.   Small place.  Try the steak tips or fish and chips.  Good music and fun.

We stopped here with the kids after a recommendation. The main dining area was full. There was a room off to the side, but it smelled like a gas station restroom. Okay....How did no one notice? There was some room on the patio so we opted for that.Lots of choices. The breakfast tacos seem popular. I went with the sweet potato hash. It was good.The wait for the food was close to 30 minutes. The crowd seemed cool except for a bodybuilder couple who kept staring at us....Yeah.... I won't be back. It was all too weird, smelly, and uncomfortable.They have a dog friendly patio.

Loved this place! It was a nice, open space with friendly people that welcomed us immediately. I ordered the quinoa and tomato salad with a huge piece of salmon. I also ordered the sweet potato fries. We came for lunch and everyone enjoyed the food and woman who took care of us. And the location is on a cute street in downtown Columbus. We were visitors to the town and glad we came here.

Bongo the manager and Precious were super nice! It's been my second time and will definitely be back! I had the Texas burger and fries and they were super tasty! The fries were crispy and the burger was moist! I had a wonderful time here:)

100% do not go here. Look I never review. This place though got me feeling some type of way. We went out on a Friday night so it's ok if it's busy but this place was pretty relaxed compared to other spots. But the wait to get a table was 10 minutes then when we we seated no one checked on us for 20 minutes. Other tabled seated after us even had their orders taken. We didn't even get a drink order in. 10 outta 10 wouldn't do again.

It's a Starbucks, folks. They have coffee, wi-fi, and various other stuffs. You know...If you don't know Starbucks, you should probably get out of your cave a little more....I really don't feel like writing any more...

First let me start by saying it's a huge open space with vaulted ceilings, so yes - it's loud! I wouldn't expect it not to be. I've now been three times - once w/my husband and we met out friends, once catching up with a friend and finally w/my kids and in laws for lunch. They've added what appears to be sound reduction panels to the walls but we were there so early on a Sunday it was quiet so I couldn't tell if it helps. The noise/bustle doesn't bother me and I can hear just fine in there.What I've loved: the homemade waffle chips w/onion dip - not usually a fan of chips/dip but they're very good. The burrata appetizer is delicious, if the soup of the day is broccoli cheddar - order it. The bucatini caprese pasta is delicious and the pasta is fresh made, my husband ordered the scallops and practically licked the plate. The steak tips were very flavorful and tender. I had the veggie flatbread at lunch and it was just ok - I think the kale is off putting. (PS - to clarify, these are dishes ordered over the three visits!)I agree w/other reviewers about the steak frites - it's not gorgonzola butter. The steak was good but I wanted the gorgonzola. I won't order that again for that reason. I think it's a good addition to the local restaurant scene.
Delicious coffee and a great atmosphere! I'll need to come back to sample the MANY enticing small bites so well displayed.

There can be a long wait at the pharmacy for new scripts but once your just refilling the drive thru window is great. Pharmacists seem to know theie stuff- especially the one at night.  I love that it's 24 hours- super convenient.
Fantastic! One of my favorite restaurants in Columbus. Wish there was a New Albany/ Westerville location.

It has a **Sephora** now so the suck level fell dramatically. Rest assured, the mall still sucks.  At least now there's reason to go.Salesman was nice.  I bought a nice watch at a fair price.  I had to wait around a while for him to take care of other customers, then I had to come back another day to pick the watch up for the discount.  Annoying but I'll return if I need to.

One my my favorite spots in all of Portland. Eat here. Eat here often. The burgers are creative and flavorful. The sandwiches are unique and delicious. The staff rules. I can't say enough good things.

The food and service was great! I had the filet and it was cooked perfectly! I also had the lobster bisque and it lacked flavor which is the only reason I am giving this place four stars. It's a little pricey but is great for a nice date night

I was really excited to try this restaurant.  We started off by ordering two glasses of Montepulciano wine at $19 per glass.  When the waitress brought the glasses, I was shocked and disappointed at the size of the pour.  My disappointment continued when I tasted the wine and discovered a the wine was good but not great. I tried to ignore being overcharged for a small pour of mediocre Montepulciano, but the irritation plagued the entire meal. The beet salad was very good. The pasta dishes were good, but I've had better. We split the beef cheek entree and it was excellent. The service was very good.  Parts of our dining experience were great, but i couldn't get past being charged $19 for a 4oz pour of mediocre Montepulciano wine   I won't go back.
The course was in terrible shape whenwe played on Saturday, it was overbookedwith no rangers out to keep play moving. Iuse to play there twice a month but not now until they repair the course.
Best chocolate in the city, beautiful cakes. My absolute favorite is the almond croissant.

We visited Oba for dinner on a Sunday night.  They have a great deal for wines on Sundays, half off all bottles $65 and up.  We opted for a pitcher of sangria.We started with the ceviche, arepas, and empanadas.  Arepas were my favorite because they were full of flavor.  Empanadas hit the spot, but I've had better in my travels.  Ceviche was ok,The one item that brought down the review was the paella.  There was no flavor or spice.  Even the chorizo was bland.  I would recommend skipping the paella.For dessert, we had the banana cheese malasadas.  They were a great finish to dinner and just the right size.Service was great, but there are other good restaurants in Portland I would visit before I come back to Oba.

The staff was super quick, accurate and friendly to boot. Atmosphere was clean and clutter free. However the tofu in my bowl was burnt to a crisp. Maybe I just caught them on an off day. I'll give them another chance since everything else was great.

Started off promising with the sun choke and spinach and bravas, but everything after was disappointing. The rice in the paella was undercooked, the flank steak was chewy instead of tender, the jambon was smoky but otherwise tasteless and not paired with anything. Most of the other dishes were oversalted, and the ahi tuna tasted off. Server seemed overwhelmed and did not ask what was wrong when food was left untouched. Food came out quickly. Maybe it was an off night because it was extremely crowded and I had heard good things.

The staff are lovely as is the food and service. This Restaurant does so much for the community of Mt Dora. Great atmosphere, romantic waterview dinning, music and good cheer at the friendly bar run by Mike the best bartender in mt dora. Highly recommend.
Excellent blue cheese burger, solid wings.  Wedge salad was good too.  Service really shined.  Very happy to have a great dinner option on West 2222.
this is one of the better tim horton's that i have been to. I go here for lunch on occasion and the service is good and food is better than most tim hortons in the lower mainland.

I absolutely LOVE this place. My first and best experience of Cuban food in Orlando. Coming from south Florida where Cuban food is its own food group, I'm critical. But this place is spot-on for me. The sandwiches, the entrees, it's all good. The croquetas I have to say though, are not the traditional-style treats you'd typically find in Miami but still delicious to me.

The cleaning has been anywhere from okay to good but it's pretty inconsistent. The customer service however was good and I enjoyed my visits for the most part. Unfortunately, Adam (the owner) tends to decide to not show up and open the store or decides to close hours before the stated closing time. I've had it happen to me now twice in the last month (a few others in the year) and each time there hasn't even been so much as a note on the door. Just lights off, no notice. If you decide to use this place, make sure you call ahead, even if the hours state they are open. Came here originally based on yelp reviews and now leaving my own.

Everyone loves this place! I DON'T! Okay, if you are gonna card everyone.. please card everyone! Not just some. My bartender was no where to be seen once i ordered my drink and food...my drink was empty...and i was dying for water..or another drink... my friend had to get up..and walk to the other end of the bar to get us a drink. After we got ours...this asshole comes back. Do we need anything? NO. Gives us our bill..tries to take it when it's obvious we are trying to figure out how much we each owe.. like come on..i know you are trying to get off work, but it's a snow storm and i'm pretty sure you were just going upstairs to sleep in your free room at the marriott. My mojito was good..but very very...light. I swear, there was like no alcohol in it.
Fantastic tacos, not fancy but delicious and very reasonably priced.  Routine take-out spot.

We have been coming to Kobe religiously each time we visit Orlando. It saddens me to see the quality and the quantity of food at this restaurant greatly diminish. Portions were cut down, chefs weren't doing the usual tricks, and the quality of food had declined. We'll probably return because its been our tradition, but will I be keeping an eye out for other Hibachi places? Yes.

My husband and I came here after going to The Oasis as it was a zoo there and we could not eat, not to mention horrible customer service . We arrived 30 minutes before closing and were welcomed in by Cristian. Let me just say AMAZING FOOD, AMAZING CUSTOMER service!!!! Like Wow factor! This place is a must if you want excellent , authentic and inexpensive food. I had the fettuccine Alfredo and hubby had the chicken parmigiana and please please try the bruschetta appetizer. The only place between Austin and Houston so far that does it RIGHT!  Leave the fancy clothes at home and go enjoy a REAL meal here. By far the BEST restaurant we came to on our weekend visit to Austin! Thank you again Cristian!!!! Please come to Houston Mandola!

This is a typical Einstein Bros. Bagels with the same menu offered nationwide.  The staff was friendly and very quick and efficient.  The place was empty on a Friday morning from 9-10:30 and I found it rather odd, given that Einsteins is a breakfast place. My wife ordered the bagel with Lox, onions, and cream cheese. She said it was pretty good, but it could have used a bit more cream cheese. I ordered the Chicken Panini with artichoke and it was very tasty.  We both ordered a strawberry lemonade and thought it was made to order, but when the attendant handed us our food she mentioned the strawberry lemonade is kept in the cooler section along with the milk, OJ, and cream cheese. My wife mentioned the place was rather cold inside, and it felt a tad unwelcoming because of it.  The restroom is a one-bloke-at-a-time type of deal, so if the place is busy, you may have to wait to use the facilities.  Overall, it was a good experience, but nothing to rant and rave about.  If you're hungry and you're in the area you can stop in for a quick meal that is slightly overpriced.  Don't make a drive just to eat here, though.  It's just not that type of place.
This review for manager Jacob. My online was done wrong I didn't get the food I ordered. Jacob went above and beyond to correct mistake and make my experience awesome..faith restored in costa Vida

Closed? Can't Be. I have to write this review as a memorial anyway.I have been here on maaaaaany occasions. How to decide if you would like the Hong Kong:1) do you like kareoke? If yes, then stay downstairs, sign yourself and your buddies up, and sing away on stage. 2) do you like dancing to pop music and whatever else you'd like to request? If yes, then go upstairs where there is a second bar and a dj spinning melodies you can groove to.Finally, 3) do you like meat on a stick? Okay, i don't enjoy myself some meat on a stick. BUT, my vegetarian friend has been known to get drunk and end up purchasing a $1 beef teriyaki on a stick from the waiters who wander the Hong Kong with these fares in a little metal bucket.How could you not love all this?

Fantastic selection of food for vegetarians.  Their guava &  cheese taqueneous are great.  Be careful when eating them as the guava jam can drip on your fingers and clothes if you are not careful.  The one complaint I would have is to ensure that they are heated evenly.  In one of the taqueneous the cheese was a bit cold.Their juices are great and fresh.  I had their mango juice - delicious!  I also ordered the vegetarian plate which had roasted vegetables.  I ordered three sides - the plantains, black beans and rice.  All were great and just amazing.  For folks that love hot food, ask for their complementary hot sauce.  It was hot, even for me!  Just a great experience overall.  I would come back in a heartbeat!

I dine at Lucca on a fairly regular basis and have never been disappointed with the food or the service.  The wait staff is great and always have excellent recommendations on the food as well as wine.Great food at a reasonable price and comfortable atmosphere.  I highly recommend.

I really like the staff and Dr. Bolerjack.  My kids are both in the process of getting their teeth straightened out.  They do a great job and I have recommended them to lots of other parents who are looking for an honest, professional, friendly staff and orthodontist.  We liked Dr. Dykes and I wasn't sure how they would do with a new Dr. but Dr. Bolerjack is great.  My kids love his approach and his fun attitude.  He makes them laugh and they no longer complain when we have to go in.

Wooden crates with plastic exterior were used to stuff the electronics into, and other things that required sturdy support to not move around and get damaged. They brought the different types of crates they had ready to be used and had us choose the ones we wanted. Thankfully the bundle we had purchased included two or three different types, and each one was for a different type of material. Clothes were put into the cardboard boxes and the fragile things were in the plastic crates with a soft interior that was custom padded. Great service.

Crowds make me nervous so I won't be dining in here any time soon, but with a little help from Eat Out In I can enjoy my favorites in comfort! I really liked the avocado fries, piping hot with a crisp peppery coating, creamy and delicious inside. The buttermilk mashed potatoes were a little bland but wonderful with a bit of cream gravy. And Wom Kim's Peach Pudding is rich and sweet and flavorful, a bit heavy but great comfort food.

Quaint little store with tons of amazing items! We purchased a cabinet from them and it looks amazing in our house. They are very helpful and always adding new inventory. If you let them know you are looking for a certain item, they will FB message you when they have new stock coming it! I like that customer attention! Makes me a BIG fan of this store. Can't wait to find my next piece.

This was our third time having Ethiopian food, but our first time at this restaurant.  We had a great experience and loved the dishes.  We had the Habesha special and added on a spicy beef dish.  The injera was soft and plentiful.  We will definitely go back and take friends who want a unique dining experience.  The staff were lovely as well!
Excellent work on a small surface (ladys watch) friendly, quick, reasonable price. Would def use again/recommend~~!!

I spent four nights here.Pros:·Great location. Walk distance to everything, T blue, orange and green line, little Italy, Quincy Market and Downtown area. It's safe to walking around until 11pm or so.·Friendly staff makes me feel like I was warmly welcomed.·Yoga mat in every room.Cons:·I live in the 10th floor, which is the top floor for customers. I always hear noise during the night, not because of the AC system or disturbing by other customers, it's a weird electronic sound, every uncomfortable.·Facial tissue is empty.PS·No free Wi-Fi for non-member customers, the price is $12.99/night for three device access.

Horrible for oil change! Set up a reservation online for a fixed time, but apparently that means nothing!!! Still have to wait for more than an hour..I went to waffle house across the street, waited in line,  ate breakfast,  got back and they still hadn't started on my car!

So glad we experienced Roe; will likely not return.  Speakeasy feel with hidden entrance to back room through other restaurant.  Gourmet food, tiny servings.  Would they hold up in larger servings?  They accommodated our Gluten Free diner with ease, but reduced our options to only the 5-course dinner.  They couldn't accommodate a fish-eating vegan, but dairy was minimal.  Wine flight was interesting, with unusual pairings; well worth doing.  Service was amazing, with lots of explanations of wine & food.  We loved the cold smoked salmon, which was new to us.  Crab risotto was another winner.  Sad to report the dessert was disappointing, so the dining experience ended with a thud, not a bang.  On the pricey side, but definitely worth a try.

We visit this place at least once or twice a year because they have delicious food.  Almost always a perfect meal - this time had a lot of gristle in the lamb meat which was hard to get past.  The other dishes were quite delicious as always.  We will return again and try another adventurous dish.
This coffee shop isn't as chic and dim lit as the coffee shops I'm used to in Nashville but they have a great product and a friendly staff...and friendly staffs are hard to come by.
hands down the best pad thai ive ever had.  always a must have for when im in portland.  very reasonably priced and very good portions.  love it.

Pros: The friendly parking lot attendant. The crab and asparagus dip is DELICIOUSLY rich. The wings are good. The beer selection is pretty great; I think I had the dragon's milk or something there. Ambience is pretty nice and dim; you don't feel like everyone is staring at you. The waitresses are friendly too.Cons: SUPER busy on weeknights. If you walk in at 7:30, expect to wait for a table. The last time I was there, we had stale chips with our crab and asparagus and asked for a fresh batch. Although my waitress was nice, she charged us an extra dollar or two for the fresh chips. Kinda ridiculous since the first batch was stale.That aside, I'll definitely come back for the food. Everything we tried (besides the chips) was delicious.Also if you have trouble finding the place, it's right across the street from Green's on Ponce.
The crab legs are on point but the price is a bit steep so if you plan on getting crablegs prepared to pay over 20 bucks basically for like a whole crab haven't tried anything else.

Grotto wasn't as hard to find as everyone said. I had the famous gnocchi. He had the tenderloin and risotto. Both were good. Really really good? No. Just very good. Perhaps my perception of the quality of our meal was affected by the service. Our waiter was really bad. Even my super-easy going companion was annoyed about it. Mike, you are really in the wrong line of work. We had actually intended to order dessert after our dinner, but after we failed to catch his eye several times over a bizarrely lengthy period of time, we opted to simply ask another server for our check. We went elsewhere for our sweets. The space was awesome. Sub-level, deep red, shabby chic chandeliers, pipes geometrically formed above us. Very cool.

Came here after reading all the reviews and was a bit disappointed. For eats, we ordered the now $2 burger (the avenue burger), sweet potato tots, wings (in the mind eraser and buffalo sauces), and fries. The burger was just ok - definitely no tasty burger, but good for the price. The sweet potato tots tasted burnt and was almost inedible. The wings were ok...the mind eraser sauce is made with ghost peppers and was pretty delicious, but as for the wing itself - I think Harry's fries up a better wing. The fries were good...definitely better than the tots.As for drinks, I had the blueberry beer and my boyfriend had the allagash white and the shock top belgian white. He liked both of his beers, but my blueberry beer was just okay. The blueberry taste was really faint - the blueberry beer is a million times better at Harry's. Plus at Harry's they put real blueberries in your beer and the foam has blueberry bits in it. Call me snooty, but I like a bit of presentation and an actual blueberry taste to my blueberry beer.

Visited this establishment for a going-away party which was pre-arranged with the restaurant however when we arrived they had no seating reserved for us.  We had all bought tickets (provided by the restaurant for that time and date)  which included a burger and a beer.  Burgers were pretty tasteless, not juicy, buns were nothing special either.  The best thing I could say about it was that the fries were hot and crispy.  Some of my friends reported that the oxtail soup was also good.  Service was shoddy however and there was nothing about the experience that will be tempt me back again.

I can't say enough great things about this service.  I don't party often but when I do, I party hard.  After a wild night on Rainey Street, I woke up feeling terrible.  The very thought of leaving my hotel made me literally wretch.  While hiding under my pillow, I suddenly had a moment of clarity.  I knew that an IV hydration service was available in Las Vegas.... Austin is a party town..... what if Austin had one as well?  Enter Rolling RevIVal.... my savior.  The bus was conveniently parked on South Congress, a short distance from my hotel.  I chose the premium service and after the obligatory snapchat videos and photos my friends took of me being hydrated, they waited for me across the street at a bar.  I hardly noticed the paramedic inserting my IV as I was chatting with Michelle.  Within 30 minutes, I was feeling utterly human.  After less than an hour, my pounding headache and nausea were gone completely. I'm not sure that that Rolling RevIVal officially recommends this prophylactically, but I began partying shortly after the service until 4 am (about 14 hours straight) and felt fabulous the following morning as well. For people like me who suffer from excruciating hangovers, this service is amazing.

This place is way overrated... Im not from the area, and my GF whos from there, gassed this place up to be something special. Went on a Friday night recently, around 8. Some lady who worked there helped us find a spot in their lot, which was a nice touch, as parking in SoBo is beyond attrocious, cars might as well be banned from parking within the city limits. We sat near the bar area...Hella loud in there, sounded like some obnoxious souls were in the vicinity. Yelling and hollering and such,I mean i get it its a a bar but it was only around 8. We get seated and waited around 10m to get a waitress to our table. Service overall was really slow. After we got our decent cocktails, another 15-20m passed before we got approached to order meals. As for the food, we decided to just get entrees. My Gf got the pork chop and it seemed to crisped on the outside, almost burnt. Her risotto was decent, but overall it was lackluster. I was gunna opt for the prime rib, they were out of it at the time. No biggie I had a lobster pie in the on deck circle...So I got it, really rubbery and quite bland. The portion wasnt that great either. Not sure why I got fries with it, but I did. The fries were ok, oversalted thought. We waited another 15m after we were done for the check. When the check came, my GF and I split the bill...For the food and service we got, this place is overpriced...I heard the quality took a dive after they remodeled it, from my GF whos been going there for a while. Seems like the place is surviving on name/prior reputation and old time regulars. I wouldnt go back. Week later we went to the Lincoln Tavern up the road, and I was blown away that place was incredible and a better value.Final note, after I ate here and checked some other reviews the night of, I stumbled across one of the restaurants customer service reps for yelp, Don. His replies were very unprofessional, belittling of the reviewer, yet entertaining, due to the fact  I couldn't believe someone who represents the establishment would write such things. I read all the poor reviews to see him go to the point of attacking the patron and accusing them of being at fault for their poor service, never seen anything like it. In this case, on a public forum its probably better to let the poor reviews stand alone, rather than make the establishment look a bush league eatery.

I am not going to comment on the food because I have been here several times and will continue to do so. So, obviously I like the food. The truffle mayo is addictive!I want to comment on the efficiency, rather lack there of. It takes a full 10 minutes between ordering and checking out. All three people who helped put my sandwich together asked me if I wanted it toasted. It seems that should be the responsibility of either the first or second person on the assembly line, not the entire team. Furthermore, the cashier is the same person that writes what you ordered on the wrapper. First of all, I am dining in and I don't need that extra wrapper. Second, shouldn't that be the responsibility of the person that wraps the sandwich at the end? The cashier shouldn't have to ask the first person on the assembly line what I ordered. Yes, I mean they asked the first,  not the person that wrapped the sandwich.Another time killer is the fact that they have to input the type of bread and cheese you ordered into the computer. The accounting of the inventory makes me think they don't trust their employees. God forbid one wheat tortilla is missing! Do the inventory at the end of the night. Get people in and out- that is in the best interest of all of us.

My wife and I went here on our first date for dinner and it wasn't a cheap one. The food was very good and rich, but small portions. I haven't been back since for that reason. Too expensive to leave hungry. If it doesn't take much to fill you up or please you, then go for a nice evening.

The people who work here are rude, rude, RUDE!!!!  I needed razor blades (which are locked up) and the person on the floor couldn't be bothered to help me get them, and then complained when I needed more time to figure out which ones were the right ones.  I will seriously never go in there again, if I can help it.  There 's a Walgreen's right across the street.  Go there instead, is my recommendation.  They take FOREVER, but at least they aren't rude.

I had high hopes for the fried chicken smothered with gravy and yes, they did come out smothered in brown gravy, but they must've been smothered for a quite while because not a spec of crispy skin was to be found--just a slimy somewhat dried out chicken. We're talking dark meat here too. I'm sticking to the fried chicken at Carver's.Still, I give Busy Bee 3 stars for being a good southern staple. Sides were excellent--collards, candied yams, and extra crispy okra.

Harvest is a fantastic restaurant for Harvard Square -- definitely my favorite in the very immediate area. Harvard Square isn't exactly full of fine dining options, and although I really enjoy Chipotle and Subway, sometimes you want a grilled ribeye with a truffle and potato puree with sauteed white and green asparagus topped with English pea greens and shaved summer truffle. I got that special for $38 and it was fantastic. The truffle smell and taste were exceptionally strong and the steak was a perfect medium rare. I also got the almond mocha torte for dessert which was very tasty and just the kind of light cake I enjoy. The bread is always good with a sesame cracker, corn bread, lemon raisin bread and a slice of French bread. I think the food is always very well balanced, cooked very well and has fresh ingredients. I'll eat here whenever I'm back in Cambridge.

It was restaurant week so perhaps it was over crowded. There is a lot of hype about Chef English and the restaurant did not live up to itThey sat us at a small bar table even though I booked 2 weeks in advance. The pasta in the appetizer was not salted properly -- is that not rule 1. Had it been, it would have been delicious - the sauce and veggies with it were really good and fresh.The lamb main dish as a kabob but it was a huge chanka meat -- come on one knows that the flavors don't permeate with huge meat chunks. Service was amateurish -- no slde plates for 2 of the 4; soup was served and we had to find a waiter to get us a soup spoon.Desserts were good.  All in All an ok place -- come on Todd you can do better --- I hope
I love that bags fly free!  I never have a problem with Southwest.  Good prices and quality service.

After my previous review I was contacted by the owner Christopher at the beginning of August. He told me how he wants to be a 5 star business and that satisfaction is supposed to be 100% guaranteed. And what he could do to make this review a better.I gave him my phone number and email as the yelp app for iphone doesn't let you see messages. I got a call on August 6th by Lisa who I can't remember is a co owner or a manager. She explained to me that the arrangement my mom had ordered came in a bud vase so it may have just looked small and what could she do to help. Luckily she was able to find the transaction and upgraded to the next size. It was delivered on the 8th or 9th and was beautiful as said my gma.A few reasons why this isn't upgraded to a 5 star:1) The woman I got who answered before Lisa was named Mary. She was sort of rude and snooty. Not very professional even after I explained that I wrote a bad review and the owner was trying to contact me.2) After I talked to my mom I realized she did a phone order. When she chose the cheapest arrangement it was not detailed as to how it would come. My mom expected something like the mug my gma got the second time around. Not a small bud vase. I believe detailed communication is key for a satisfied customer and consumer when placing a phone order.3) I got a phone call on the day of delievery questioning if my gma was home. She is in a walker and hard of hearing. I asked Mary if he rang the doorbell and she said yes. After I called my gma and called back Mary she had said he left it with the neighbor. Umm Hello...how do you know the neighbor       A) will give it to my gma      B) keep it  and pretend nothing was delivered  I know the delivery guy did not ring the doorbell.
