When she found out I was only looking TO BUY 2-4 chairs, she told me she would NEVER split a set and waved her arms around in seeming random fashion to tell me she has individual dining chairs for sale somewhere in the store.  There are some beautiful pieces here but I think their refurbished furniture and reproductions are overpriced .  I don't think I'll come back to this store.
Really enjoyed brunch here. Fantastic omlettes, local cheeses, unreal bloody Mary's great service!

Just left after having lunch here and I will NEVER be back. More than half way through our meal one of the waitresses brought a plate of RAW meat and placed it in a table close to us. Raw meat! Out where your customers are eating a meal. The meat sat on the table for at least 20 minutes with customers walking by it. This is 100% a health code violation. I will never eat here again.

On a pre Boston Calling Sunday adventure a friend of mine and I were trying to go to Al's.  However' Al's was closed, along with about a dozen other lunch spots in the area.  Seriously, why is everything closed on Sundays?Anyway, we opted for Saus, and I thought it was great!  The atmosphere of the restaurant is cool and artsy.  All of the food is made in house.  Everything is really fresh!  The food was excellent:  I had the Legit Corn Dogs and a regular order of poutine with bacon bits and egg on top.  As for sauces (hence the name Saus), I went with Bacon Park, which was great, Vampire Slayer, which was good, and Colonel Mustard with the Wrench, which was also good.  This place deserves to be 5 stars, but I have one complaint:  the ordering process and seating area is awful.  If it's remotely busy is extremely difficult to move around and/or find a seat.  If you're getting take out, then you're making the right move, because Saus has 5 star food.
They have the best mac and cheese and great service! It wouldn't be my first choice of restaurants but given the chance I would go back!

YUM!  Unlike everyone else in Boston, I blew off the esplanade on the 4th and opted to sit at Croma and eat and drink coronas.  I definitely made the right choice.  The patio is great for people watching, which there is TONS of on Newbury St.  My friend and I shared the bruschetta appetizer which was fabulous.  I also recommend the ceaser salad - but beware they serve it with anchovies on top.  Ewww.  The service was excellent - we had a really chill waiter that didn't mind that we took up his table for 4 hours (though I'm pretty sure our tab was worth it!)  That doesn't mean it was pricey - everything was totally reasonable.  The pizzas are amazing as well, so you pretty much can't go wrong with anything on the menu.

For the money enough variety and freshly baked bread to make it a go-to place for nights when there isn't time to get dinner and go to your next activity. Especially good for breakfast. Good coffee bar, especially the coffee.

I've been to many massage therapists. I have never had what I would consider a BAD massage... But this was, by far, one of the best massages I've ever experienced! Jasmine is not only very well trained, she's one of those rare therapists who just has a knack, an innate sense, of where you're hurting and how best to work out those sore spots. She listened to me describe where I was hurting, but also addressed areas I was completely unaware were sore until she worked her magic! She'll adjust her pressure, but I didn't need to ask her to, as it was perfect from the get-go. There have been times, more often than not, where the therapist will make me secretly wince. I've always just dealt with it, as I've assumed that it was the only way to get the deep tissue tightness addressed. I didn't secretly wince with Jasmine... And it's a week later, and I've never felt so good a week out from a massage! Give her a shot! I promise, you will NOT be disappointed! And I'd place bets that if you try her out and you're someone who likes to have massage work done regularly, she'll become your go-to massage therapist!

The absolute best Ribeye Steak I've ever had!! The flavor was delightful with a fresh chimichuri  sauce! -it was cooked to a perfect medium-rare. The service was spot on! Our water took the time to let us enjoy our appetizer and drinks before bringing out our meal. The timing of the entire meal was perfect. I will definitely recommend this restaurant to all I know! -Excellent service, and wonderful food!!

The reviews for this place astonish me. Maybe I've been on off days but I have been here twice in the last 3 years both times the same disappointment. Firstly lack of options makes me assume what is offered must be of quality but this just isn't true. Both times I received warm or should I say hot pearls in my tea that made the cup warm to even hold. I don't know of anyone ever wanting a hot sugary drink. The last time I threw my cup in the garbage just outside. This place is busy often with line ups. Probably because of its good location with lots of schools around. Teenagers are less picky on sweets often.

Golini Painting did a great job. We hired them to repair horsehair plaster in our house, which is from 1900, and they did great work. They showed up within ~1 day to give the estimate, and then emailed it to us right away. The painting part of the estimate was a little too expensive for us, but the plastering they did is really excellent quality. I'm pretty sure they used blueboard with a coat of plaster over it and the formerly crumbling walls are now mirror-smooth and immaculate. They also did a ceiling where the previously peeling paint couldn't be fixed, and it's now perfect. They came on the date they told us, did all the work between 7am-12:30pm, cleaned up everything when they left, and they even patched two smaller holes in the wall in a bathroom for *free*!! We appreciate their work very much!!

First time for me.Went to see excellent movie Hell or High Water. I would have been happy watching it in a garage.The seats are narrow and do not recline, blah...The audio/visual is first rate.As I always say I can endure anything once with a full bar in proximity, bingo!The movie was A+ and the bottle of rose bubbly made the seat much more comfortable.

This place has foosball and shuffleboard. That is awesome. Good beer selection and the bar tender was super friendly. But don't eat here. Super weird menu and nothing was even close to worth the price. I got the smoked meats plate of mystery meat (no one seemed to know what meats were included) for $12. It came with three small pieces of each the of meat. The flavor was okay, but it was served cold. Cold pork tenderloin and wild boar (eventually someone told me what the meats were) were weird and kind of gross, unless your into cold smoked meat. The smoked sea bass tasted just like beef jerky, if that gives you some idea of how over smoked it was. I could only bring myself to eat one piece of each meat.
Reserving a space here was extremely fast and easy. Samantha was really helpful and super kind. She explained the rates which match what was online. I would definitely use this space again.
This was my first time here. Food was great but both our meat dishes were way oversalted. I'm still rating high as the rest of our food was great and service was fantastic.

Best pizza place for hawaiian pizza! My Fiancé and i have been eating here everyonce in a while since our first date almost 6 years ago.  The quality is great, the customer service is on point.  I recommend this place to everyone! :)

Been here for about 1.5 years now. - excellent value - i had my 550 sq ft apt for $825 since early 2013 and rent has not increased for me.  - location is a mix bag.  (the good -- edge of travis heights, a very safe and uber rich neighborhood of old hedge-fund hippies;  its like 20 minute walk to south congress and overall close to the center of all things.  the bad -- nothing except one bar within a  close walk -- everything is residential [but the bar is fun]; not near public transit bus lines]- the pool and hot tub are large and excellent- the staff is really, really friendly, impressively.  - the tenants are a mixed bag -- depending what you are going for -- it really seems like 90% of them are white kids just older than college age, and just younger than having-a-family age [these days thats a rather large gulf].  What this means is that there will be a fair amount of partiers and socializers, although the apartments are by no means rowdy or loud.   i've met a middle-age single woman here once and talked to her about her experience, she was understandably feeling out of place.

Counter is in my humble opinion one of the top three restaurants in town (Jeffrey's and Fonda the other two). Especially now that they offer valet and have a liquor license.  Food is extraordinary. Service is professional and unobtrusive. Portions are small and tasty so make sure to order the 7 course. It's a food holiday!

The portion size was smaller than I would've liked, and the food wasn't really distinguishable from other Thai like Madam Mam's.That's not a bad thing. Madam Mam's is good. What made this two star was, while mistakes happen, my dish was extremely spicy. I really love spicy food, I have a pretty high tolerance for it. But eating the dish (T1) was almost devoid of any enjoyment. It upset my stomach slightly.What's WORSE, is that I'm almost positive I obtained food poisoning from eating this dish. It was the only meal I ate that day, and now I'm up at 5am writing this because of it. when it came back out, it was also quite spicy. Probably won't be back, but I suppose it could be a fluke.

What has happened to Figs? We used to eat at the Charlestown restaurant every few weeks and always enjoyed it. Then we took a break for a few years and returned for the first time last weekend. The restaurant is filthy, the service was absurdly slow and sloppy and the food was miserable. The calamari, long a favorite of ours, was rubbery and almost flavorless. Our pizza, half Red Sox and half Bronx Bomber, was soggy, greasy and tasteless. Unless we hear of a major transformation, We won't be back again, even in a few years. Do yourself a favor. Skip Figs.

I can't believe there is only one review of Fresh Pond park so far. This place is very nice. We lived in Huron Village for about half a year, and came to the parks for walks very often. The place is dominated by Fresh Pond, and there is a circular path looping around the water. Go all around will take you about an hour, give or take depending on your speed and mood. There is nothing stunning about the place, there is no fancy landscaping or breathtaking vistas, but it does give you complete relaxation while you are here. You'll find many people walking their dogs, joggers, and walkers.To get there by public transport, take one of several buses in Harvard Sq that go down Concord Ave (#74 comes to mind, but there are more). The adjacent Huron Village section of Cambridge has nice walking routes in and of itself, in particular Brattle St, with a selection of nice restaurants also so you can recharge after your stroll in Fresh Pond.If you want to make it even longer, you can continue walking along the Charles River on Mem Drive, which is not far, or go to Mt Auburn Cemetery, which is also close and completely amazing.This area of Cambridge has a lot to offer if you're looking for a relaxing weekend day to amble around and enjoy yourself in a mellow kind of way.

yUM !!!! Oh man. Can't go wrong with the Pollo Ciao Bella. Chicken and mushrooms in the most delicious freakin sauce. And you get a choice of pasta on the side or veggies and potato. But seeing as it's an Italian place, you should go pasta. I had the Ciao Bella pasta with linguine. So flavourful. We had garlic bread as an Appy. I know how basic garlic bread can be but this was soooo garlicky and perfect. Highly recommend. Atmosphere was great. Some guy sat at the piano playing all night. Service was wonderful.

This was the best service I have received in a long time. The food was to die for and the atmosphere is so welcoming. This was my first time coming here and I will most definitely be coming back. I'm someone that never makes reviews on these types of the things (yelp) but, I am so impressed with this establishments that I had to share my thoughts on how GREAT my time was here.

Red fucking Velvet cupcakes, people.Yum.Yum.YUM!However....at $2.50 a pop (and they are smaaaall) a wee bit over-priced, I think, but it wouldn't stop me from getting more of their delicious cupcakes.
Best quick grab and nom place. Awesome gyros. These guys Crush it! Would recommend to friends and family 10 out of 10 times. Blaze and graze baby.
The food is ok...but the drinks are the best i've ever had in my entire life... Soooo yummy! Love it!

Got a large pizza and a salad for take out.  Pretty good compared to most pizza places in the area, but it wasn't the greatest thing I've ever had either.  The salad was average, and the price was decent for the size of the pizza.  Almost 4 stars but it was a little greasy and wasn't cooked completely right

An awesome little place, in a really nice part of Germantown, with awesome food.  My family and I went here for lunch, with tasty results.  Portions are large and hearty-- I had the buffet, which is a great value for the money if you love German Sausages.  When you get the buffet, you also get a discount when you purchase one of their delicious desserts.  My family ordered the hot pretzel nuggets, which are fried, delicious, and tasty, especially with the honey mustard sauce they serve it with.  Generous portions, and not oily at all.  The original sausage sandwich was huge, more than enough for my sister and mom, and was served with a hearty portion of spatzle. The buffet saw a number of side dishes, including green beans, cabbage, bean and ham soup, mac and cheese, red cabbage, German potato salad, sauerkraut, and several salad items, including applesauce, a green salad, and bread rolls.  While the sausage stew tasted a little strange, it wasn't too bad, and the buffet had 5 different types of sausage.  Everything was freshly stocked and tasted great.  Note that when you pick up a buffet, you can buy a dessert (normally $4-$5) for $2.50.  For dessert, the four of us split two cream puffs-- one chocolate, one vanilla.  These were GREAT.  The cream was rich and soft, and there was definitely no cutting back on the good stuff!To top off the whole affair, service was terrific.  Parking is easy, and it's definitely a memorable experience.

The first time I ordered Spartan Pizza is really a love story. I was working out of state and my partner, under quite a bit of stress, hadn't gone to the store in a while. I took to the Internet and searched for the finest sandwiches in the land and there, like a beacon of hope, was the recently opened Spartan Pizza. I ordered a sandwich to be delivered and to this day, she considers it one of the best sandwich moments of her life. We've gone back for sandwiches a couple of times and always enjoy them. I recently got a pizza for the first time and loved it too. The staff is super cool and very nice. I'm already looking forward to my next Spartan experience.

Papi's is right near our house and we had been meaning to check it out for awhile.  We had heard good things...sadly we didn't experience them.The highlight was the first thing we had, the Caribbean milkshake.  It was epic deliciousness.  After that, straight downhill.  I ordered a Papa Rellena for an appetizer. It was pretty bland.  We were excited about our entrees, ordered the daily special, ropa vieia, and a papi's specialty, masitas de puerco.  The ropa vieia was decent, nothing special.  Moist but oversalted.  But it was amazing compared to the masitas de puerco.  It was tough, dry, and bland.  Barely edible.  The service was slow and uninterested, actually sitting down at a table near us to text for 10 minutes, but he does get credit for noticing we barely touched the masitas, and he comped it.I'd like to give Papi's another shot. But probably won't be back in a hurry.
Loved their vegetarian menu! The margaritas are delicious, guacamole is ok, staff is friendly and the ambience takes you back to Puebla, Mexico! Oraleeee!
Excellent and authentic comfort food.  After years living in the Middle East, I come here when I get homesick and need proper hummus or mujadara.

**parking is free** that's a big deal! The staff is friendly & the atmosphere is fresh & inviting.  Had dinner here food is delicious although I've had better fried rice, and the crab rangoons had a tad too much cheese filling.  Overall I'd come back for sure knowing what not to order. Great fast chinese. Goooo

I went at 11:30AM for lunch and found a parking meter ($1/hr) nearby. It was hard backing out on Guadalupe, but doable. I ordered a chicken sandwich & americano. The sandwich was great. My coffee never came, so I had to go and remind them. Good experience, good menu, friendly folks. I will go back.

Curious with the increased road congestion leading to this food market, I decided to check out this new asian fresh food market. It only opened 2 days ago - so some of the items were not priced yet and aisles not fully stocked but the store was already quite busy with customers. I was lucky to find a quick parking spot amongst the chaos that ensued due to the poorly designed exits and already terrible road traffic that occurs near that area/intersection. Note: there is roof top parking available!Upon entering the store, you can feel the largeness and huge selection of asian goods. Large dedicated areas to fresh Seafood, Meats, Bakery, Dairy, Produce, Sushi Bar, Frozen foods of all kinds, Hot food area (serving dim sum, duck and more) and the inner aisles packed with a variety of asian sauces, noodles, snacks, drinks, etc... Essentially it reminded me of a hybrid T&T and Pricesmart.Prices seemed comparable to other supermarkets but there were some cheaper items as well. Of course, shopping around and knowing your prices will get you the good deals. Everything in the store was nicely organized and clean. Items were displayed in a meaningful way and produce looked fresh and well stocked. There are washrooms available and cashiers were friendly and efficient. Overall, nice alternate place to go grocery shopping but I'll definitely be avoiding this area during the weekends because parking and even driving around this area will be painful.

Quick and reliable service, and conveniently located in harvard square. I used their wifi adn got some work done while I waited the ~25 min to get my screen replaced. My phone has been good ever since!PS there was a giant dog there the day I went--not sure if I just got lucky, or if this furry friend is always there--but it was quite possibly the cutest (and laziest) dog I've ever met. I'm considering going back just to visit with the dog...

Very nice hotel. I usually stay in $$ or $$$ hotels, and this one was a solid $$$$. So I can't accurately compare this hotel with similarly priced ones. But  I have to say, it was a real treat. The room was well stocked with everything we might need. They served us a lovely welcome tea, and every employee we encountered treated us with an easy graceful friendliness. My only slight disappointment was that there was no coffee maker in the room.

Low grade sushi for cheap.Experience:The wait can be long, but they expanded the place so now it moves.  Food:I used to think this was a great place for sushi, because the quality was tolerable and it was cheap.  However, now that I'm older I would rather pay a little more for good quality food.  I value quality over quantity now.  So depending on what you're looking for this may or may not be the place for you.  If you get the platters you get a decent amount for the price, but be aware that it's poor quality sushi.  I don't recommend the sashimi here for that reason.

Want a tasty burger in a more upscale environment, but don't want to resort to a chain resto-lounge or shell out the big bucks for the fois-gras-filled version at Gothams? Then Romer's may be a place for you!Came here with some friends because my boyfriend was raving about it.  We started the short rib poutine and the onion rings, both of which were very rich and tasty.  I ordered the rib burger a little hesitantly, as my fellow yelpers seemed to have different opinions on it.  In the end I was happy I ordered it, it had the right amount of juiciness and crunch to it, and satisfied that meat craving that I was having.  My friends tried the Wicked Cheeseburger, the Ranch Star burger, and the Kobe Beef burger (looks like they've reduced the price from $24 to $20).  They were all similarly satisfied with their burgers.  Some previous reviews were critical of having burgers well-done, but I actually prefer them this way anyway (there's a difference between well-done and overcooked, unless we're talking about slabs of steak).Service was pretty good and attentive, and we didn't have to wait too long to get a table or our food, so it looks like some of the kinks about service have been resolved, at least on our visit.
Just go and find out! Be sure to drink way too much and over tip the staff!
I'll never shop for pet needs anyplace else.  The people at this store are first-rate, Kayla and the groomers are wonderful, management and employees are caring and wonderful.  Kudos to all of you.

I really feel like I'm in Portland when I visit this bar. Bartenders - Amazing! Vincent is the MAN! The Girls - Depends on the day. Sage and Valentine are unbeatable... but some of the others 8{ This bar is just like a woman; So AWESOME sometimes... then other times... It is a must for anyone wanting the full Portland experience regardless of the staff on hand or the night in question.A Unique Portland Experience!

Have been to this little store on Burrard street many times before, the staff is always nice and very helpful while trying to put an assortment of items to fit in a size box I wanted, will be going back anytime I need a nice gift for Birthday or just because....price range for a nice size assortment of multiple items $150-200

I love the guys at Arrow Paint. They are always friendly and helpful and they never complain when I walk out with fistful of color swatches. I admit a small addiction to the sample pots of Benjamin Moore paint. Our living room was a pretty cool patchwork of about 15 colors before I finally decided on one. Thanks to the guys at Arrow for helping me find the perfect color!

On a neighborhood Facebook Group page, I read a notice that Chuan Lu Garden was opening an outlet in East Orlando.  I hadn't heard of the place downtown; but, the notice generated a lot of excitement.Stopping in today, that excitement spilled in to the restaurant, as patrons were lined up at the register to order To-go items.  This is not your typical Americanized-Chinese take out.  Yes, they have lunch specials, which we ordered; but, they also offer BBQ Skewers, a dozen different soups, Chinese Hot Pot, dishes with Chicken, Duck, Vegetarian, Beef, Lamb, and, Pork, as well as specialty items like Jellyfish, Pork Belly, and Lobster!Today, we ordered the Shrimp in Black Bean Sauce; and, the Beef in Szechuan Sauce.  Both came with Vegetable Fried Rice, and Egg Roll and choice of Soup Won Ton for my wife and Hot and Sour for me.The soups were okay - very stingy on the pour, which didn't even fill the to-go cup.  The egg rolls were just barely passable (full of cabbage; but, no meat); and, that's being kind.  BUT, the main dishes were incredible... The sauces were thick and unctuous, and so very tasty, the vegetables crisp and fresh; and, the meat cooked just right; and, not a bit overdone.  Neither of us could stop ourselves from devouring every bite!Would I come back?  You bet!  Would I get the lunch special? Probably not... There are simply too many other things, which seem of much more interest!

The tacos were freaking amazing!!! Omgggg this is the first authentic taco place in Boston that I can find with well seasoned meat, spices, etc. Soooo good. I tried a chicken, carnitas, and shrimp taco. All very good, even the chicken. I usually don't order chicken, but it was actually tender with flavor. The hot sauce was a good amount of spicy (But it is optional). I come here way too often. Lol they should launch a punch card program

Very dirty and old hotel.... everything was sticky and worn down.... and the breakfast was a joke... you can choose some bread or someWaffles .... the staff are friendly .... but overall definitely not a good experience... will not be back

This place is pretty rad. Although the wait is very very long. We waited almost 40 minutes to get seated on a hot summer day, and decided to go to the park nearby. But it is a pretty amazing spot for brunch. We ordered a lot of things, but I ordered the vegetarian egg white with chicken sausage added. It was a very delicious meal as I cook something of much lower quality than the dish. The pesto and broccoli rabe really mixed well together and would recommend the dish.The fruit bowl is pretty large and can feed 2 people at least. The cocktails were also interesting. We got the espresso martini which had a very sweet yet milky flavor that made it perfect to combine with brunch.Also people say the love muffin is the best thing, but it tasted way too buttery for my taste. Overall the place has a lot of options and the drinks are interesting, but be prepared to wait in line...

How can anyone not like this place? The food is great! If you have never tried the pastries, coffee or gelato you are missing out. The service is amazing! it has serve yourself soda machines, but the help is so good that they will come out and ask if they can get you more soda and run over and fill it up for you. I actually only have one negative comment....I wish you would change the bread. Just a plain sliced Italian bread would be great. The other stuff is oily and yucky. We always skip it. Keep up the good work! We come in every Friday :)

I've been to several of these chains before, but I appreciated this one much more.  The ambiance ranges from elite to jack and cokes at the bar.  Thanks to our bartender (Blee? Your accent was so thick!) we had a great time.

The best breakfast spot to get French toast and scrambled eggs with cheese, yummy and they only accept cash but there's a few bank around to withdraw...the staff is the friendliest but the food is great.

Honest and dependable.  Chris was running late, but he kept us updated and insisted on keeping his appointment.  We thought our garage door might be acting up and making funny noises.  However, in less than five minutes, Chris told us that all it MIGHT need is lubrication.  He did that -- and programmed a tricky remote opener all in under twenty minutes.  Quick, dependable, and honest.  That's what you need from a repair person.  And as an added bonus, he's a local business.  Give him a try.  You won't be disappointed.

I absolutely love this salon! All of the employees are sweet, not to mention stylish.I have been going to see Laurina for a few months now and she is wonderful! She's great at what she does, listens to her clients, and is honest. I won't go anywhere else or see anywhere else. I highly recommend this salon! The customer service here is fantastic, they really know how to make you feel at home.

I didn't have high expectations because I thought this place might be a tourist trap.  I had some crab eggs benny, which substitutes crab cakes instead of an English muffin.  It's good, very crab tasting.The service attempts to be good.  They lost the order because we initially sat outside and asked to be moved inside when the weather got worse.  They must have thought we were angry because they called us afterwards and asked. In short, the food is good.  It's a worthwhile place to eat if on Granville Island.

We went on Black Friday - the first day it was open in Buckhead. It wasn't crowded but they didn't have the bar stuff together yet. We did get a small comp. to compensate. Still a great feature for the holidays.

The food is fantastic! I had never been there before but heard great things. I tried it the other day and brought my grandmother after a doctor appointment. The ambience was a little vibrant for the elderly lol. She complained about music being loud but I enjoyed it! The food was incredible and the Nutella milkshake lives up to the hype! 5 stars :)
I know this is an uppity restaurant with a chain feel, but the food is delicious so I can't not come here!  The vegetarian options are awesome and the spices are perfect!

I had a groupon (12 for 20) and decided to give it another go. However, the costs will come out to around 20 dollars per person. I ordered a beef combo and my friend had lamb. Both had very small meat portions and the veggies were just ok. Adding to that, I was very unsatisfied with the sauce bar option (no peanut butter sauce) and the spoons for the condiments were so tiny! It was not worth the price even WITH the groupon. I would recommend you to try 89 hot pot. About 26 dollars incl tip for UNLIMITED hot pot. I don't know how they're still in business tbh.

4.5/5 for Ambiance 3.5/5 for service 4/5 for menu - taste and portion sizes. Overall satisfied because after the initial delay the server scored points for sharing our sense of humor. Tried some sheep cheese (ok) Jamon(ok) Kale salad and sautéed shrimp (good) ceviche (very good) and some olives (pass it). Will definitely recommend to friends and ask management to add more servers to busy shifts and bring some more variety to the menu.

Just....just eat here.  You wont regret it.  Even on a saturday night, the line was long but seemed to move really fast.  We were seated and ordered almost right away.  It helped that we looked at the menu before sitting.  Everything is seasoned very well so all of our food was flavorful and delicious.  The chicken in particular was moist, crisp, and surprisingly not as greasy as one might expect from fried chicken.  The fried green tomatoes were also delicious.  Some of the best I've ever had, nice and piping hot.  Will definitely come back, especially to try the pies, if we're in the area again!

The food was very good and service was quick.  You will love the friendly staff.  If you are in the area check it out for good home cooked food.  I had late brunch meal.  I plan to check it out for lunch and dinner.  Only complaint:  tea needed to be sweeter.

Oh, Phara. You don't disappoint. The slower than usual service can, but you should know that their servers do not section their service, are tending to a lot of large parties with separate checks, and don't work off a POS system (eek!). So, prep yourself to practice patience and give the servers a little credit. BYOB, love this. Mezza Sampler, love this too! And it's a toss up between the Lamb La Zeez and Shwarma Plate -- you can't go wrong with either. But do order lamb as it's their specialty! The last two times I've dined they've sold out of their Lamb Roast Special. Nomnomnom.The belly dancers don't disappoint. Quality people watching when this really gets going.Great place for large groups or a twosome. Let's get some mister fans out back!
LONG WAIT!!!! Very difficult to check out even though we already had a reservation. Hidden and added fee. I WILL NEVER USE BUDGET AGAIN!!!

Absolutely love this place.  This is the quintessential local video store.  May it never die.  The place is small, but has everything you want.  It survives b/c of people like me, people who can respect the small business and go there not only to get a movie but to support a greater cause.  I plead with you all to support stores like this in your local community, b/c one day w/out our support they'll all be gone and replaced with mega walmarts, and if our kids don't get to experience stores like this it will be a shame.

I may have gotten the fridge I was promised for the price agreed on but nothing else. I had to help delivery guy, Marco, to drop the fridge from the PU truck. If I hadn't been able to help him I'm not sure he could have done it himself. Then once installed the fridge was missing the butter tray door and fasteners to get the moulding on the front in place. I do not remember the latter appearing in the showroom so I think it was a bait and switch deal. I called twice and got a hold of the same guy and the first time he said he was too busy and the second time he promised to have someone out that day which never materialized. So in the end its probably better to spend an extra $300 to get a new fridge with a warranty and Austin $50 exchange rebate. Also on the receipt they gave me there was no company name, address or phone number. What does that tell you?
Exspensive for what it is, good options, decent food.

Just had their sushi burrito and wow... SO good! I don't think I'll be able to go back to regular rolls again. It was incredibly fresh and the combo was amazing! I now have a new addiction lol. I ordered the Samurai Dragon burrito, yum!!!
Excellent service. The food is on a different level. Everything exceeded expectations.

Metrovino looks any other generic upscale Pearl restaurant- pleasant enough, but not a lot of character- half-full. However, I've been a few times now for dinner and have to say that the food more than makes up for anything/everything else. (I'll get there in a second- but I'd eat this charcuterie board beside a garbage dump if I had to).The charcuterie board here is among the best I've ever had. Everyone raves about it- and yes, it really is that good. Great variety and presentation- duck sausage! chorizo with quail egg! I may actually be drooling just thinking about it. I've also had the beet salad and the broccoli- both are well-executed.For my mains, I've had the salmon, halibut and the duck. Of the three, I'd say the salmon was the best. Very fresh/moist and adorned with ratatouille. The halibut was good, but not really a stand-out. I enjoyed the duck, which has a great hazelnut romesco which is an interesting taste combination- the peach is also a nice compliment. Delicious.Both times I didn't make it to dessert- but plan to eventually!Huge, extensive wine list- some pretty interesting reserve bottles you can drink by the glass.The service was good- some decent recommendations. Perhaps a little bit slow for the fact that it wasn't particularly busy.
Small portions, small rolls. Rice is not properly cooked. Not enough ginger.Smells like piss inside

The boyfriend and I had brunch here yesterday morning.  It is conviently located right next to Trader Joe's on Sand Lake.  We made reservations for Sunday brunch at 11am, though our reservations were likely unnecessary.  There were probably less than 10 tables occupied when we arrived.  The restaurant had an indoor/outdoor set up.  All of the sliding glass doors were opened up so we were technically inside, but you felt like you were outside.  It was a nice day so this was a great vibe, and clearly everything could be closed up on a cold or windy day.  I did keep my sunglasses on for most of the meal though, which some might consider rude, but due to the indoor/outdoor nature of the restaurant I wouldn't be able to see otherwise.  I ordered a specialty cocktail called a Spring Fling.  It was delicious, light, and refreshing.  It tasted clean, pure, and earthy.  I really enjoyed it.  I also loved the giant ice cubes that came in it.  I love big ice cubes as they don't melt as easily and prevent my drink from becoming watered down.  For an entrée I had the pulled pork with eggs and spoon bread.  The portion was large.  The pork was delicious.  The bbq had an apple flavor to it that again contributed to that sort of clean and fresh taste that ran throughout the meal.  The spoon bread was insanely good.  I love spoon bread and this was some of the best I've had.  It had a nice delicate flavor, and was just the right level of moist.  Some spoon breads become soggy and others dry, but this was perfect.  The eggs were good, but not special.  I had mine scrambled instead of sunny side up which is the way they recommend them.  My boyfriend ordered the servers recommendation of brisket with basil pesto eggs and potatoes.  The potatoes were so good.  They had a nice spice and crust to them.  I literally ate one.  My boyfriend was not sharing anymore!  The brisket was good and had an awesome sauce though I don't think it was quite as juicy as my pork.  Finally, his eggs had a little more panache for sure, but something about green eggs makes me feel like I am in a Dr. Seuss book.  Finally, on a friends recommendation we ordered a breakfast bomb.  We didn't need it.  We had plenty of food, but it sounded too good not to try.  It is a biscuit stuffed with spicy chorizo and topped with cheese.  It was delicious.  It was also larger than expected.  With my small appetite I could've ordered that as my entrée.   This restaurant is farm to table and everything tastes fresh and homemade.  Even when the food is rich and decadent you don't fee like you are eating unhealthy here. If you are in the area, you should definitely check this place out.  I know I'll be back.

Moving to Vancouver from the Northeast of the US five years ago, I had just about given up on finding authentic Caribbean food here - Havana, further north on Commercial was very disappointing. Varadero just changed that.Just looking at the menu we were pretty sure we had come to the right place, but even still, the food itself surpassed our expectations.We ordered two empanadas (one cheese and one beef), the vaca frita (fried shredded beef), and the Cuban sandwich. All were exceptional.The empanadas were first to come out and were amazingly crispy with very flavourful fillings. The cheese was amazingly gooey without being 1000° in heat. The beef was moist, tender and packed with flavour.I started with the Cuban sandwich, and it really hit all of the notes you would want: crispy (but not overly toasted) pressed bread, a nice slab of melted swiss cheese, and wonderful roast pork and ham. Probably one of the best Cuban sandwiches I've had. It should be a simple sandwich without much embellishments and Varadero's was spot on.The vaca frita was the surprise hit for us. We substituted maduros (sweet fried plantains) for the tostones (fried green plantains) because well... maduros are amazing. The beef itself was like nothing we had had before. The shredded pan-fried beef was packed with spices and full beefy flavour, and despite the dry appearance somehow was moist and tender. A mystery.The rice and beans served on the side was fantastic, as were the guava and mango sauces served with the meal. We had a couple of cortaditos (sweet Cuban espresso drinks).Overall a fantastic experience. The food took a little while to come out, but that was clearly due to fresh preparation, which showed in the quality of the food.Will be coming here again and again, and with a fairly decent non-meat menu for a Caribbean place, I can even bring vegetarian (and maybe even vegan) friends.

These guys are great! They are very personable. I had my tire replaced here for so cheap. They even checked out my tie-rods for me and said I should replace one of them. I had them do it. The quote was amazingly affordable. I drop the car off in the morning, and its ready after work...unreal! ALSO! when I go to pick up the car, they fixed my exhaust for free! no more rattle! ALSO ALSO, they topped off my power steering fluid which always leaks...I will go back here for pretty much everything the car will need...you should too!
The scrambled egg tortilla (I always get it sans avocado) is the best! It's a wonderful breakfast to take to go.

Check in process using the Magic Express was good - only gripe was having to sit and wait for the bus to leave the airport for quite a bit longer than anticipated. Beautiful grounds and buildings. Housekeeping was excellent throughout our stay. The kids really enjoyed the pools. Several restaurants on site but all over-priced - but Narcoossee's was the best food I had anywhere at Disney. Given the opportunity I'd stay here again.

I recommend the chicken wrap with BBQ sauce! Really good. Especially with the bottomless fries (if u get the right waiter who will give them to you). Service is a crapshoot depends who is working. Can be great,  can be bad. Food is always good American fare. Burgers are good too of course. Stay away from the arctic cod sandwich ... Very dry. Food is always good consistently, except for that cod sandwich.
The good- $1 beer on Thursday nights, drunk college students, boys singing Nsynch and Back street boys, dj upstairsThe Bad- Not too many people dancing upstairs, $7 for drinks,

Words cannot describe how wonderful it was working with The Potting Bench staff, especially Karen. She helped me choose flowers that were a part of centerpieces for a 50 th wedding anniversary party.  Karen was able to describe exactly what would fit with my 'vision' and created beautiful flower arrangements. Everyone at the party commented on how gorgeous the flowers were. I'm so appreciative and thankful for the arrangements that added so much to our event. I will come to The Potting  Bench for all of my flower, design and nursery needs!A+++

We've used Bridge City for 4 or 5 years. Some of the teams have been better than others, and given the business, there is some turnover. Overall, we're quite happy with them. Our house is clean, and because they send a team, they are in and out quickly. I work at home, so that's a significant consideration for me.I've had a couple of fantastic individual housekeepers over the years, but I've also employed a few stinkers. Using an agency takes the anxiety out of hiring. Bridge City's crews have been efficient, thorough, and courteous. We have some special instructions about our floors and cats, which they follow. I have also found it easy to deal with their office. They're responsive on email, which I like.

i was extremely pleased with my piercing experience at...well, piercing experience.  i met with christina to discuss my inner conch piercing.  she explained 3 common locations and which would work best for my ear.  she was very personable and extremely helpful in selecting jewelry and a gauge for my piercing. the piercing room was clean and the entire piercing process was quick and relatively pain free.  with jewelry the total for the piercing came to $73 + tip.  a little pricey, but definitely worth it.

The FOOD...AWESOME.  The PEOPLE...AWESOME.  The REVOVATION...BEYOND AWESOME.  It makes the place look bigger without sacrificing the coziness and charm that has always made it an Austin MUST. I swung in for dinner and asked if the renovator was available for other jobs.  They told me it was the owner and her shear inventiveness. I'm south American and no stranger to Argentine cuisine.  Beautiful authentic space!  LOVE IT!

Never been to a Panera before but it was what I expected.  Mostly soups, salads, sandwiches, and some basic pasta dishes. The bread was very tasty which is what they are known for I suppose. It was super busy at lunchtime but the food came fairly quickly. Pretty sure the Panini sandwiches are pre-made.A bit on the pricey side but nice comfortable atmosphere. Great if you want a light and tasty lunch!

I'm so excited to have a place like Snackboxe near BuHi. I've tried a handful of dishes and most of them were excellent!The one reason I give 4 stars instead of 5 is because I do think some of the dishes are severly overpriced for the amount of food given.Food (worth it)I have so far ordered:- Papaya salad (Laos Style): OMG this was spicy. I love spicy food but this was spicy even for me. If you do not handle spice well, do NOT get it Laos style. I'm not sure if the regular style is as spicy. I LOVED this papaya sald. It was funky in all the right ways and left me tearing up but I love the burn.- Beef larb (ordered it regular and rare): TIP! You can order the beef larb rare, essentially making it like a tartare. It is so full of flavor! I will probably always order this when I go. It feels super fresh and healthy because of all the herbsLemongrass ribs: The ribs had great flavor and are pretty big. So $8 for 2 might seem like a lot, but the ribs are bigger than typical ribsNam Khao: Crispy coconut rice salad with fermented pork. Okay. This dish is probably hands down my favorite. It has great texture and flavor and every bite has me love it more and more. And it's not as bold/funky as some other dishes so this is a great one to share if not everyone has the same taste/love for strong flavors. Food (okay)Herb fish: Okay, for $8 you get a tiny bundle of fish that would fit into the palm of your hand. It is wayy too overpriced for what you get. And I thought it tasted okay. They added some shrimp paste or something so it gives it an even fisher flavor which I was not loving. Saku: Tapioca dumplings. I did actually like the taste of these. You get 8 balls for $8 which is not a bad deal. But they also kinda fall short flavorwise considering how bold everything else is.

We had the good fortune of stumbling upon Jenny when she responded to an online inquiry.  Now, we are happy to pass along our recommendation and share what makes Jenny a treasure.Of course, we were drawn to her outgoing personality, strong organization skills and her keen awareness of the market.  We met when we considered a big change to a Townhouse.  Jenny was very aware of our wants, needs, overall 'wish list' and 'won't compromise on' list.  She never applied pressure or tried to convince us of something that wasn't a good fit. However, she shined brightly when we listed our house in Brookhaven and immediately went under contract.  She knew us well and our home.   Those details were reflected in the marketing materials.  She was masterful in her efforts.In both cases, her knowledge was impressive and her ability to be readily available.  I now know there are some tight turn-a-round periods on documents.  Jenny's expert guidance and unwavering patience was critical and incredible to navigate us through the complex process of buying/selling a home. There are only good things to say about Jenny.  Including, she is smart, savvy, dedicated, resourceful, hard working and an honest realtor.  We would (and do) highly recommend her!

This place serves a really mediocre dinner.Fish and chips were actually quite tasty, not too much batter, two large pieces for $15.The steak frites though was terrible ($18). I asked for no frites and extra salad. The salad it came with had a really yummy dressing, but it was -drowning- in dressing, an inch at the bottom of the bowl excess. Instead of extra salad, they added some baby greens and blueberries to the board (see photo uploaded). It wasn't dressed at all, and there were only like 5 blueberries but they were in really rough shape - why not just leave them out instead of serve subpar food?It was also a poor cut of steak, and although cooked well (medium rare), it was super chewy, cold by the time it got to the table, and too salty.I'd give a 4/5 for the fish and chips, a 1/5 for the steak frites, like seriously just don't order it. And a 4/5 for the ambience, it's brand new inside and cute decor. I think it's more of a brunch or glass of wine sorta place, the food is amiss.

I had a great and easy time using this service. I sent a message over yelp to inquire about pricing. I was sent back detailed pricing within 30 minutes. Natasha and Ruby cleaned the bottom half of my 5 bedroom house that I share with 4 other roommates. This was a task just not up to everyone as you can imagine. I came back home after going out to lunch and the house is absolutely spotless! They listened to what I needed cleaned the most and did it very efficiently. They also use safe and organic cleansers. I would definitely recommend Maid for Portland :)

I really like the booth seats where you take off your shoes and sit like you're sitting on the floor. Never experienced that before. Fun element.The nigiri was nice and thick. Totally worth the money. We got yellowtail and salmon. Delicious. I think the only thing that threw me off was how many rolls had honey mustard on it. I guess I'm just not used to that being on sushi. It tastes fine but there were just an overload of items with honey mustard of top for my liking. That and crab salad. Nonetheless they still had plenty of items that didn't have those two ingredients to choose from. Excited to come back.

The burritos are the best I've had in ages!  Not greasy or full of sour cream and cheese (although that can be good too), just fresh, wholesome and friggin delicious.  I get the veggie burrito that comes with grilled red onions, black beans, sliced avocado, dark lettuce and deliciously seasoned rice.  Quite a generous size too.  This place is tied for my all time favorite burrito.

Great cupcakes! I tried several flavors (the carrot had a bit too much cinnamon for me, but most people like that), and on a whole I found them to be comparable w Sweet, which heretofore has been my cupcake standard in Orlando.

Wonderful experience dining here on a Friday night. We were celebrating an occasion and I have some food allergies -- after speaking to manager Randy on the phone earlier in the day we were completely taken care of, including a great table to view the rest of the (small) dining room and complimentary champagne upon arrival. Oysters were delicious as expected, but the seared octopus appetizer was as good or better than it looked. We went with the traditional lobster roll and Bacon Lettuce Lobster Tomato sandwich for dinner. Both delicious and well portioned. Bonus points for the restaurant doing a great job spacing out the food. We never felt rushed and really savored the dining experience. Would recommend to anyone for dinner, and suggest heading across the street to jazz bar Beehive for a night cap when done.

Trivia nights are cool but other than that this place is, yet again, an over priced over pretentious bar.  $13 just to walk through the door and $7.50 pints. This place was in it's prime before the Dummy Donnelly group took it over.Get over yourself, Lamplighter.

I haven't order food from you guys in Years and now I know why. My tacos sauce container was open and all over my food. The tacos were too burnt. My 5 yr old brother couldn't eat it.  Deliver took over 1 hour.

Their cookies were huge, for only costing $1. Additionally, their club sandwich is big enough for two meals and were really tasty. I had to get my meal to go, so the toasted bread got a little soft, but that's understandable. Their Yankee pot roast soup was amazing, perfectly seasoned, although I don't think their were enough chunks of vegetables, still very good and reasonably priced.

When I walked in your restaurant I was expecting great service, and I received the worst in return. Maguly Sanchez was not only the rudest most  disrespectful employee I ever came to encounter but she then was rude to the gentleman behind me with specific dietary restrictions. First time coming to your establishment and I will not be back. She the had the nerve to call us customers names and assume we didn't know what she said. She should become a little more worldly and learn Spanish speakers don't all look the same.She is a very unhappy and misguided person who needs to leave her personal problems with the people she has them with and not with customers. If it was not for your other employee who was great with helping me (Reno Cubides) it would have been a lot worst. She clearly has a problem with accepting money from customers. But no worries I won't ever spend any there again she has certainly guaranteed that!

Last week was the second time my coworkers and I called in our lunch order for pick up.  Both times the order was $60-$70, a nice amount of business for this restaurant.  Both times during the order we confirmed when the food would be ready (20 minutes).  The first time we were in the restaurant at the 20 minute mark ready to pick up, but our order hadn't even been started.  We waited another 20 minutes before everything was ready.  Disappointing!  The second time, we didn't leave our office until the 20 minute mark, giving them a buffer and ensuring our order would be ready as soon as we arrived.  Again, when we arrived our order hadn't even been started being made, this time 30 minutes after we ordered and 10 minutes after it had been promised.  We waited another 15-20 minutes for our order to be ready.  Not acceptable.  The meal itself was decent (perhaps because by the time we ate we were ravenous!) but not that great.  Factoring in the unacceptable wait and lack of apology with mediocre sushi, I don't expect to be back.  Definitely not recommended for take out.

A friend and I were visiting Austin for the first time (during early December) and were told by hotel staff and multiple Uber drivers that we needed to see the Trail of Lights. After having dinner nearby, we walked on over to the trail (we couldn't take an Uber there since so many streets were blocked off). We headed over at around 9:30pm on a college night (this means no tickets were needed in order to enter, so the event was free). It wasn't as packed as many other mentioned in their reviews. This is most likely because it was freezing (I'm from NYC, so trust me when I say that it was EXTREMELY cold. It even snowed a few days before) and also because it was so late at night. Because it was so cold, we had to rush through the trail. The walk up to the trail was long so we were cold on the way up and were anticipating another cold walk back to the street where we could catch an Uber.The lights were beautiful and there are a ton of Instagram-worthy photo opportunities here. If the weather was warmer, this would be a perfect evening activity for families with children. There are also stands here serving snacks and hot beverages, but with closing time approaching, many of them were shutting down.My tip is to go slightly earlier and on a warmer evening so you don't have to run through. It also may be worth it to drive and park nearby although I'm not sure how much they charge for parking.

I visited Bartaco today for the first time and I LOVED it. I will definitely go back. I initially said I was only going to get a small bite to eat since I ate not too long before going to the restaurant with friends. I ordered just one chicken taco and the corn (I asked for it off the cob).  It was amazing !! The corn was just ... I can't even put it into words. I would go back for the corn. The taco was also really good and for $2.50 it's a steal. The food was so good I ordered the plantains... Again OH my gosh. Just amazing and fried to perfection ! They came with this creamy sauce that added so much flavor. I then got another chicken taco, and a fruit skewer from the kids menu. Needless to say my small bite to eat turned into a lot more. I would give BarTaco 5 stars except for the fact that I had to keep reminding the waiter for things I asked for which wasn't a lot (a straw and a kids menu). I had to ask at least 3 people for a straw before I eventually got up went to the bar and got it myself ... There goes that 5th star. But regardless I would definitely be back! Ps: the complimentary valet parking is great !

If you are on dirty 6th and want to see a live band on a Friday night come here and have a look.  I have wondered (okay probably stumbled) in here many times and have not been disappointed. My recent trip,I did get a drink at the bar  with no problem. However, on other occasions, it can be hit or miss. I believe it just depends on the what band is there, how many people in the place, and if understaffed. Hmmm..maybe just like any usual bar on any night of the week.

We were hauling a trailer, and had to do a narrow turnaround on a busy street. One thing led to another, and we jack-knifed the trailer into the back of our new car. Took it to VIP, and had the parts in over the next couple days. Took it in, and 1.5 hours later it was done! Great prices for labor, super friendly staff, and really great work - good as new!!!

Granted, it's fast food, but I like it and I especially like the staff. One such staff member, I believe her name is Megan, is always enthusiastic and working hard to ensure you get your order. Keep up the good work!

My wife and I both have been going to Shear Creations for almost two years. I love the quality of service and attention to detail. I cut my short this past year which is super scary but Denise made the process easy and my hair looks so cute. Added bonus,  they now  a glass of wine with a cut and wifi.
This office (Westlake location) is the ultimate - in professionalism, efficiency and regimens tailor-made for my particular concerns. I highly recommend this location.

Why travel all the way to Portland when you can get Voodoo Donuts in Austin. This place is a must, especially if you have a hankering for late night sweets. Voodoo Donuts is open 24/7 and has a broad range of flavors, designs, and tasty donuts to satisfy your sweet tooth. Several donuts will make you scratch your head and wonder what they must have been smoking to come up with such a concoction. For being in such a tourist-y area the prices were very reasonable. One suggestion is to make sure that you have cash as you can work through the line faster by going to the cash only line.

This review is in regards to my experience with Oak + Fort's online website, more specifically, their Customer Care department. I can sum it up in one word: nonexistent. I purchased a gift voucher online as a gift for my bridesmaid back on August 31st. I would have purchased it in person at their downtown Vancouver location, but as I had been busy with my wedding and I had flown in from out of town that week, I simply did not have the time. I thought I had saved myself so much time and effort by purchasing a gift certificate online. I couldn't have been more wrong.They only accepted PayPal for payment, which wasn't a problem. I received the receipt for my payment right away, but it wasn't until September 9th (more than a week later) that I received an email from a Stephanie from Customer Care confirming who she was to send the voucher to. I responded on the same day, requesting that she send the voucher to my email address so that I could then forward it to its recipient. I never heard from anyone again. I sent another email on September 12 (nothing), and on September 17th I told them that if I didn't hear from them by the end of the week, I would file a dispute with PayPal to get my money back. Throughout this time, I attempted to phone Customer Care (no one responded) to deal with this issue. I also made sure that the gift voucher did not get lost in my (and the gift card's recipient's) email spam folder. I finally got so fed up, I went ahead and filed a dispute with PayPal on September 20th. One week later, Oak + Fort had still not responded to the dispute, so I escalated the dispute to a claim to get my money back.It's a shame I've had such a horrible experience with Oak + Fort because I really am a fan of their clothing and aesthetic, along with their sister company, Loft82. But for a company with a continuously growing online presence (Facebook, Instagram), it's  frankly pathetic how bad their customer service department is. I even tried writing on their Facebook page in the hopes that SOMEONE would see and respond. It's unbelievable that they have no problems updating their Instagram and Facebook accounts daily, but no one can even be bothered to respond to messages in their Customer Care department. Even more, for something as simple as purchasing an online gift card where it is to be received by email (and not even through regular mail), it's inexcusable that it's taken this long without a reply. It's been over a month, and as of today I still have not heard a single word from the company since September 9th. I will provide an update if I ever end up hearing from them to see how they handle the situation.
Great place! Quality food, clean, and the staff is very friendly. Family run and they make you feel at home. J,M & S your parents should be proud!!

Such great sandwiches and bread...Quite rough around the edges, salty and blue collar, without a hello or an excuse me, Lambert's says I'm not gruff enough to wait the lengthy line. But it's absolutely worth the experience.
We've been going for takeout here since I can remember. Even as a little one I remember loving it! They've always been so nice and polite and very quick with service

I like Thai, but live far north.  Thai Cuisine is the best option for good Thai food, good service, and a nice atmosphere.  The family that owns this restaurant is great, too.  As long as they keep doing what they're doing, I'm a fan.

Came here after the oasis disappointed and was much happier at this location. The views are great and the atmosphere is relaxed and not overcrowded. We ordered food and drinks at the bar and sat outside. My Cuban was a massive and a little spicy. Other food was ok, better than downstairs. I got a side of truffle fries and sweet potato fries to share. They're pretty big too but why would you want less? Large beer selection and recently acquired liquor license. No waiter service so had to keep getting up to get tap water. Altogether a nice place to watch the sunset and chill out.

Solid movie theater. The seats are comfortable and clean. The sound could be a little better, but overall a solid movie watching experience. I don't recommend going on opening weekends though as they have a lot of kids in and outside the theater that talk/txt during movies and just hang around outside. I only go to the Alamo Drafthouse for opening night movies (they make sure people don't talk). If you're catching a movie during the weekdays though, Cinemark is great. No student discounts which is disappointing.

If you want a great meal , great service this is your place. This is a small , low stress place that you can actually relax and have a nice meal with friends. If you like the current trend of large trendy restaurants that thrive on chaos and mediocre food then this is not your place.  The fish fry they do on Friday's and sometimes Saturday's is absolutely the best. They use Haddock and it is cooked perfectly. The meatballs are excellent ,  garlicky and the right mix of meats and homemade. The Fra Diavolo (spicy) red sauce is fantastic, I get it with broccoli and garlic and it is so damn good . Truly everything I have had there has been great. The chefs John and Mike actually care about what they cook and it shows, the care and consistency they show every time we go there is astounding. I love this place. This place serves real homemade Italian food in a pleasant welcoming environment a very rare thing in Florida.

Really disappointed by the recent financing fiasco. Their business hours are short and the online ordering system is closed until further notice. I had purchased a year membership and barely got any worth out of it before things went downhill. Since I tend to work late, I relied on their online ordering and delivery. I'm also typically unable to make their now-reduced business hours. I want to feel sympathetic but I can't deny that I felt like I wasted my money with the membership.
Food is good but I feel slightly over priced.I only come for the waffles, because they are awesome and I think their price is very reasonable.

Ok, i tried this place for a third, and last, time. Here is why I wont go back. Ordered the Italian Sausage with linguini. When the dish arrives (Salsiccia con Pepperoni ), it is in a bowl sans linguini. I try a little, looking for linguini...it tastes very good, but no linguini. I finally flag down my server and explain the menu says with linguine (I actually had it pulled up on my cell phone). He looks perplexed and goes to get the menu. He then points out the menu and it doesnt mention linguini. Then I notice its in the antipasti section. I make him turn to the entree section, and wa la, there is my dish. He apologizes and says he will correct it. Now, at this point, I am ok with all this. Mistakes happen, even though I dont know why the dish is listed with the same name on the menu in two different places and why he would assume I want an antipasti as my entree, but he should have known the menu and clarified. But here is where it goes south...they bring out the dish, I eat, he brings the bill, and states they would only charge me for the antipasti. I didnt need them to do that, as I ate the entree, but nice gesture. When the bill comes, they charge me for the entree. I dont argue, I just want to leave (I had been there almost an hour). Then, about an hour after I get back to work, I have a bout of Veronas revenge...so after three mediocre meals here and gastroentestinal distress, I will not be returning. Shame too, as I use to eat at the Carabas that was at this location many many times.

I love this deli. Tucked into a strip mall between a mattress store and a ladies dress shop, I didn't expect much. But the more I explored, the more I discovered. Lunch meats and cheeses, salads and pickles, halvah by the slice, handmade chicken and pork sausages coiled on the counter, bread that is still warm on shelves in the back or racks up front by the cashier. Pastries coated with whipped cream and frosting in a refrigerated case, and dumplings and other mysterious things in the freezer case. I usually ignore the grocery shelves, but it is an interesting anthropological expedition to peruse the aisles (for a NW native like me).The German bread is wonderful (not labeled so you may have to ask). Add some of the chicken or pork sausage, a bit of cheese, the beet salad and you have an excellent lunch. They are always busy and you must wait your turn, but the people behind the counter are helpful, if not overly friendly. If you have questions, they will find someone who speaks English.

our flight from ny to boston was cancelled, they made us wait over an hour in a baggage check line, nobody came out to address us, they didn't pay for anything, we were also charged another baggage fee on the way home the next day, I will never fly American again.

Yikes, I can't say anything about the delivery, but this is based off walking by numerous times, and yesterday, coming in to purchase a discounted bouquet. The cute gypsy girl inside was friendly and chatty. She and I discussed the fine art of flowers on a broke heart (my roommate's), and she bagged them up for me. The flowers I looked at were marked down to $5 each. Probably left over Valentine's Day flowers, I still wanted something to brighten the apartment for a little bit. The store itself is nice and tidy, with lots of displays. Some of their potted plants seem a little pricey, but it's a small business and not Home Depot. I'd stop by again for flowers for sure.

Good crepe and vietnemeesecoffee. Sadly, first time there from LA and my friends purse was stolen from this location. Keep your belongings next to you at all times. Some shady individuals roll through there.

Fun frozen yogurt place.  Tasted rich and not like yogurt at all,  We had the chocolate yogurt with peanut butter sauce and peanuts and pistachio and cream with fresh fruitCrazy amount of toppings, but most importantly peanut butter sauce!

Yes, it is not cheap here - but it has a great, scratch menu and TONS of wines by the glass, thanks to their great system. This is not for cheap happy hour types (get over happy hour, will ya Portland!!! do you need to get something cheap to justify a night out?). This place is for people who appreciate great ingredients, and well-prepared, creative food AND a fantastic glass of wine to go with it. The salmon gravlax carpaccio is the best I've ever had. The gorgeous sea scallps were perfectly done and served with a poached duck egg and lots of other accompaniments - $29 - but the plate is complex and anyone with food knowledge can tell that a lot of time went into it. You pay $30+ for a boring steak and some uninspired potatos and a bland veggie of the day at most places in town. I will be back soon!
Excellent! Perfect fusion of sushi and burger!!!  Highly recommend all American burgushi and deliverance roll.

I've been to this Smyrna location twice-both times for lunch.  The first time I enjoyed the buffalo wings pannini.  It was very good.  But this time I decided to try the chicken salad pannini.  It was horrible.  Chicken salad?  More like chicken paste.  The chicken appears to be ground up into a paste.  The Panini bread was cold when it got to my table.  I am glad I ordered a cup of gumbo or I would have starved.  Our waitress had to be hunted down to get some mayonnaise which I thought might help this chicken paste.  It did not.  The chicken salad is horrid and I would not recommend it.   The service today was not so great and our table was wobbly.
The service was fast, waiter and staff were nice. I feel the pasta was over priced. The flavor was good.

I popped in to Abode for lunch today.  Intent on ordering a fruit bowl, I instead stayed and had the Laska chicken and rice dish.  I enjoyed it immensely, and wished I could have more. The staff was attentive and was able to easily accommodate my dairy allergy. When I return this summer to Vancouver, I plan to stop by again!

I love this PLACE!!!!! That's all I can really say I have been going to this place for almost 3 years now, and still haven't got sick if it. If you truly want to try real ethnic Indian food, this is the place to be! The decor of the restaurant is beautiful and modern...very unexpected. The service is amazing. The food is soooo gooood. I would recommend Kadahi Lamb and butter chicken and for veggie dishes shahi paneer or alu gobi. Although everything tastes delicious. Drop by this place you won't regret it. PS: they are opening another restaurant in downtown soon.

So this is a relatively small dining establishment. Probably could squuze 50 or 60 in... may be more if they were friendly types.You will find a lot of standard items... tacos and taco salads, burritos, enchiladas, fajitas, quesodilas, Chile replenish, tostadas, tamales, and more.They also have some interesting things like the seafood soup.In our case half the group arrived an hour before the rest! They provided warm tortilla chips and a medium heat salsa... a lot of both.At least no one was bored.In my opinion, they accommodated special orders better than I imagined.I have heard others report concerns but I am generally satisfied.. and at times quite pleased, with our experiences

My heart belongs to Ohlin's when it comes to classic donuts, but as I neither live nor work near Watertown, Doughboy is good for a fix! What a $1.30 donut should be. It isn't Doughboys first rodeo, and it's the better for it. Simple, friendly, local, with no pretension. They have all the classics, but the Boston Creme is the best. (A close second how's to the mini Boston Cremes...adorable.)Unless you're a die-hard Dunkies fan, please don't go there. These donuts are so much better!!

Please do something Playland!  Such a great place.....been going here for years. And like the Canucks, it needs a major facelift. The roller coaster, the log ride, and the hellavator is the core of this park. The atmosfear is a great new addition.The music express should be part of this list but mostly now the ride is short, doesn't stop then go backwards like it used to. It was a ride worth waiting for. The pirate ship, the scrambler, the swings are all older mainstays but good nonetheless. And if your going to have these older rides Playland, then the Octopus should be there too. The rest of the park is mostly un-amusing.Playland, you have an awesome space in an awesome location. Get rid of half those crappy rides (starting with the other coaster) and bring in some non-spinning fun stuff that make you think before you go on.I will pay more for better rides.  Im a big supporter of this place.  Keep changing.

yes, you get what you pay for; here it is though; i have stayed here, only 23 miles away, just as a quick get away....never had a problem with the swimming pool; yes very thin walls but the smells all depend on the room you get; try and book one on the third floor...noise runs from top to bottom....i would never stay on floor one, esp during busy times or weekends......this floor seems to be in really nice shape ; i mean, what do you want for $50 per night?? i have stayed in much worse places for more money.......
Good tuna salad sandwich but the sandwich maker doesn't wear gloves when prepping food. Places needs a good cleaning.
Whoa - tasty! Love it. Ordered the Basic Ramen in miso base, added spicy meat option with soft boiled egg, and Shazam - tasty!We'll be back.

This company drives me nuts! It's a RECYCLING company in PORTLAND that still relies on paper invoices, and snail mail. No online bill pay, no payment over the phone by credit card, and no paperless options. It's the only bill I still have to pay the old-fashioned way. Grrrr.
Had takeout last night, chicken fingers weren't cooked and gross.  Crab Rangoon's tasted like they were made last week. Why can't you get good Chinese food in South Boston!!
Wonderful Boston Italian restaurant.  I had the Cape Oysters and they were excellent.  Nice selection of wines and not over priced.

Ugh this place.  I've gone here twice for private events, so have really only been in the downstairs part, but have been unimpressed overall.Can't really nail down exactly what it is about Dillon's that rubs me wrong; maybe the pretentiousness of the place - high ceilings, boring decor, awkwardly dim lighting, just a lack of character I guess.  Seems like the bar is trying to be classier than it is, I guess; I felt out of place here and then realized I tend to feel out of place when a bar lacks as much funk as this one does.  Just not my scene (clientele-wise, too), really.Drank beer which was fine, really just nothing to write home about.

We just had two closets done by Closet by Design. Terrific experience all around. We were worried about the company because of the bad reviews on here but turned out fabulous. Angela, the designer, was promp, made a great design and was easy to work with. The installers came on time, finished in two hours and cleaned up beautifully. The closets look and work great.

As good and unique of a meal I can remember having in a long while: Terrazas Reserve Malbec, Duck & Oyster Gumbo, Stuffed Quail with Sweet Potato and Collard Greens and Peanut Butter and Chocolate Mousse. Service from Justin on point and personable. Pretty much perfection front to back, top to bottom.

Only place I trust to wax my eyebrows! They are the best, all the ladies in my family go to First Class. They stay busy, which means that I can't usually walk-in and get my nails done, appts are a must, which doesnt always work for my busy schedule. Love this place!
This is a super cute, friendly shop that sells yummy gelato (and donuts too). The bright interior always puts a smile on my face and I love, absolutely love, the painting on their wall.

Twice I have been here and twice I was absolutely delighted from start to finish. The service here is the best. They are all attentive and make me feel like a VIP, even the guys refilling my water glass.Our first trip was with a reservation and that went very well. The waiter made some great suggestions from the menu. The chef even sent a gift. It was  a delightful taste of something that could not be found on the menu. The fried avocado appetizers were the best though dinner and desert were also spectacular.Second trip we did not have reservations but luckily we were able to enjoy a meal at the bar. We enjoyed burgers this time and they were great. Again the service was tops.This is a great place and it makes date night with the hubby even more special. I can't wait to go back. Thank you Roaring Fork!

Vegans!!! This is a hidden gem on Main Street! TONS of vegan options; smoothies, coffee, tea and bubble tea! Including soy, rice, almond, coconut and hemp milk! Organic is a big deal, too and Gaia Java gets it right! Plus, 80% of the pastries are vegan as well ~ right on! I highly recommend swinging in, alone or with a group. Fantastic atmosphere with amazing artwork for sale... Will definitely be coming here more often :o)

This is a great summer after work spot.  It's sad to see people write negative reviews of this place!  The food and prices are great but it's pretty much about the atmosphere.  You're outside, on the docks with music playing and it's all good.  I love coming here on Friday nights.  Hopefully the loud music keeps the 1 star yelpers away from this place.

I actually hadn't been aware of all the drama surrounding Saus' attempts to get up and running, but now that it's there, I can't think of a better call for the middle of one of Boston's busiest bar districts than grease and sugar to the wee hours, with or without a Belgian accent. The two most important things about this place are the fries and the waffles. Anything else is gravy (literally so with the poutine). As it happens, the fries are among the best I have ever tasted anywhere -- maybe I'm a little biased by the fact that the French fry in general is in a pretty dire state these days in many places, but these crispy, reddish-brown fries are epic. The waffles are pretty nice too -- you could easily eat one or two of them for breakfast, but the sugar crunch combined with the popover-like egginess screams dessert. The staff is very friendly, and service drags a little but only because the food takes time. I'd like to see a few soups or something like that added to the menu eventually, but it's hard to argue with what they have already -- it's certainly a big step above the McDonald's down the street.

I went in after parking downtown just because it was close, and I wasn't looking for anything specific. The yogurt BLEW ME AWAY, and my friend and I got another one. They have so many flavors, and each flavor is intense! I highly recommend it.

Il Piatto is a great neighborhood Italian restaurant near my house.  I've been coming here for years and never had a bad meal.  I really do not understand the bad reviews. I think it's the closest in Portland to the food I ate in Northern Italy.
I lovvvvveeeeeee the people here. They're always friendly. The place is always clean. And the food is amazing!!! YESSSSS.... EVERY TIME. Did I forget to mention that they're a BLACK owned:))

well this place is less than 4 mins from my house.  Whenever I am house hunting...I go by two things...how far is the nearest grocery store and liquor store.  This Kroger is well maintained, and while I have found several expired items on the shelves from time to time, the mangers will promptly get rid of it.
