Dr. Nik also explained everything that was happening as I got my teeth cleaned and when I got my fillings. I also got my choice in music during these procedures which was rather calming.

Had the mushrooms skillet and the Coca (chorizo on bread). Both were tasty. But the flavors do not mix, in case you are sharing. Ordered tea and coffee with a waffle (pistachio and rose water). Also very good. The wait is long, an hour and 15 minutes, but the host is pretty good on estimating the wait, so just go window shopping on Robson.  For our visit, the staff are friendly and efficient.

Overall this place rates average.The Occidental beers are solid, not the greatest but very good lagers. Decent representations of their respective styles.Urban German food is decent. The schweinebraten, though, really needed more seasoning, and the gravy was a little weird tasting. Braised cabbage and mashed potatoes were average. Bratwurst was OK. Fries here are beer battered and crispy, but not for everyone.Ordering at the bar, getting condiments, bussing your own table, and not very friendly bartender kind of takes away from the experience.That said, nice looking space, though it is really loud inside, with a nice patio/deck area and a nice view of the St. Johns' Bridge.

Found them thanks to everyone's rave reviews!  Very friendly, quick, and affordable!Since I don't have to get emissions tests very often, I will only be seeing them once a year, and their awesomeness actually makes me look forward to my next test!

CHECK YOUR RECEIPT! I work close by and my co worker and I each order a chicken BLT salad 5 days a week there, their salads aren't cheap but they're good! It's always the same order grilled chicken BLT salad with no bacon and with goat cheese.They have occasionally messed up my order which is understandable because everyone makes mistakes. However the last 3 days they haven't been able to get my order correctly! They will charge me for the goat cheese I requested but they don't put it on the salad, and when I called in the girl told me that they were out of it but couldn't explain to me why they charged me for it nor did she offer me a refund for the item. The next day I'm over what had happened the last two times and i decided to give them another shot. For the third consecutive day they messed it up by putting bacon in the salad. I'm absolutely done, my co worker and I will take our 12 dollars each and buy lunch elsewhere.

YUM! There's only 6 flavors available at once. My friends and I didn't realize that it would be inside a Philly house? Anyways, it was a short walk from our hotel so why not? $5 for one scoop seemed a little obnoxious but you won't want more than one. Super savory. I got the salted caramel, delicious. My friends got pretzel, strawberry and melon. All were yummy. The strawberry is similar to a strawberry mentos flavor versus a traditional strawberry ice-cream flavor. It was delicious either way.

They are very friendly and very nice , they never have problem there , & already prepared their foods when they go to the drive in area . Their boss ( manger ) should give all the employee A A+ 100 for doing a excellent jobs.

Quick service, but overpriced for what it is and its ambiance. Not really a relaxing place, but this airport terminal has so few food options. Had the fried shrimp, which was good but not worth 23.99...

Look and Feel:  Rise from the depths of the subway into the hubub of downtown crossing and you'll feel like you've entered the biggest outdoor mall ever made.  Maybe you're right.  The subway lets out directly into the famous Filene's basement.  Shops are everywhere, and the streets have few cars, and are lined with bricks.  Most stores in the area are definite chains, and the ambiance tells you so.  That said, it's a nice outdoor mall.  And after shopping, lunch in Chinatown could be so good!  Restaurants:  Like any mall, there's an indoor, neon-lit food court.  This one features a passable mediterranean place.  Avoid the food court, however, and head the few blocks away to real food.  Shops:  Many varied, and excessive.  Filene's Basement is a good time.  Shopping is a sport, and this is fenway park.  Marshalls a block away has less expensive, arguably cheaper merchandise.

This resort offers the most unique experience at Disney World. The lobby is a gorgeous dark word cavern with African inspired art work. The pool has a water slide, a tiki bar, and plenty of lounge chairs. The room had bunkbeds for the kids and a balcony overlooking the savanna. In the morning, I had coffee while gazing down at herds of wildebeest,  giraffe,  zebra, gazelle, and kudo. There were also ankole cattle, red boar, cranes, and ostriches. The restaurants and lounges are all very nice. The shuttle and bus services are fast and convenient. The only negative about this resort is that we had to check out of it and return to our real lives.
Easily best taco in Austin. Be patient, it's worth it. The pastor is heaven. For $1.50... TAKE MY MONEY

Another one of those places I've been going to forever - 14 years I guess.  Consistently great salsa and queso.  The queso flameado is good but tricky to eat.The best enchiladas in Austin are here - the San Antonio Plate.  It's cheese enchiladas with carne guisada on top.  Damn damn good - perfect Tex Mex.The fajitas are good - a bit too much of the onion and bell pepper for me, but the grilled tomatoes are a nice touch.   Great guacamole, pico de gallo, tacos, charro beans, chalupas and more.   Amazing flour tortillas. Always very friendly service - a very traditional, homey South Austin joint.

This place needs to franchise out! Wonderful concept and great food! A must if you like clean food. They grind the meat every day. They use beef with no hormones. The veggie burgers are great! The produce is farm to market fresh. They also have a great bar and they make sure you have a drink in hand right away. Gotta love that!

I am not a vegan but wanted to try something new. The food was great! On the suggestion of the gentleman who took my order I had the shrimp Poboy with a kale salad. It was excellent and very flavorful. I will definitely be back as I try to figure out this healthier eating lifestyle!
Quick, cheap, good quality eats. I got the pork kimchi and grilled shrimp tacos. Both had a ton of authentic Korean flavors with the spicy kick! Super cheap with my total being around $7.

Groupon brought me here for a deal for a simple cut, style, and conditioning. What I got was all that and more:* Courtesy call to say they were running late and asking what time would work best * 50's - 80's music in the background * Fun, clean, and casual environment* Simone (stylist) - asking what I want, talking about options, then whipping out her magic (with no pictures or anything) Bonus pts: * Daryl adding A little make-up do on the house! Overall great experience if you're up for the spontaneous and unexpected. really friendly staff so come with a listening ear or story to tell. Highly recommend!

They don't have this in Oklahoma! This was my first Lucile's visit and I am determined it won't be my last. We sat on the porch during a chilly rain and ordered the wonderful coffee and the homemade chai. It was perfect with the beignets, although I was fuller than I wanted to be when my food came. The biscuit was amazingly light and didn't even need butter, just a bit of the wonderful strawberry jam on the table. My husband ordered Hank's eggs and ate it all! The spice was not overpowering, but prominent nontheless. I had the Cajun breakfast: red beans with meat, two poached eggs topped with hollandaise sauce and served with cheese grits. It was heaven! We went the next day and I ordered it again. Be ready for great food, friendly service and close atmosphere. Enjoy!

Ate there last night after giving this place a one year rest. Level of food and service were back up to a high level--just like the old days when we came here 15 years ago.  Clam chowder was amazing, rock shrimp were tiny but tasty. Fried oysters were cooked perfect. I'll start going back

My first time here and NOT my last for sure :) I was very impressed how nice they were. I liked the size of the bike shop and all the Cannondale bikes(kinda obssesed with those bikes). I got there at 6:30PM and they close at 7PM. They changed the tire on my bike so quick! The service was outstanding and they seemed very knowledgable. My bike was on very good hands :)I definitely recommend this bike shop to everyone :)They have all the Garmin GPS (I wish I knew before I bought mine from RSC), they have amazing cycling apparel, shoes and MORE!

I'm a little bit sad about giving the Barking Crab 3 stars. I've only been here once before (last summer) and I have these amazing memories of the seafood. I was so excited to come back on Saturday and dig into a bucket of mussels. The appetizer I remembered had been just that: a big bucket full of mussels in a delicious sauce. This time the appetizer was a smallish bowl - the mussels were fresh, but I didn't LOVE the sauce. My friend and I split the crab cake sandwich as our main meal and it was pretty good - I think she may have liked it more than I did. The service was fine (our waitress drew a cute little crab on our check haha) but I really hated the table she sat us at. The table was held up by thick bars and I just happen to hate sitting on stools. Also, the table had some pretty big gaps in it so I was neurotically worried that my drink was going to spill. Being uncomfortable and anxious can definitely put a damper on any meal. Still, I do love the atmosphere here. The Barking Crab really reminds me of some of my favorite seafood shacks in Long Island. I'm sure I'll come back again but I'm definitely more eager to now to explore some of the other seafood options Boston has to offer.

On my quest for the best non-chain delivery pizza in Boston, I found Il Mondo. It currently occupies the #1 spot.I'll start with the bad: Delivery takes a long time, and these pies are fairly expensive. Delivery (which I request through Foodler) takes about an hour, which is longer than my hungry stomach would like but pretty typical for delivery pizza around here. At about $22 for a large, Il Mondo is not a bargain. That said, it's less expensive than Crazy Dough, which is its main rival for the Amy B. Pizza Crown.Now on to the good--the very, very good. The buffalo chicken pizza is out of this world. It's generously topped with chunks of buffalo-marinated chicken and drizzled with ranch (my favorite). I'm into chicken on pizzas and so have also enjoyed the chicken with roasted red peppers and spinach, but I keep coming back to the buffalo chicken. The crust on these pies is on the thin side, so be forewarned if you're a thick crust junkie.The pizza, in fact, is so to my liking that it pains me not to give Il Mondo five stars. But the price and delivery time are both just high enough that I can't. In any case, this is pizza I will keep on my speed dial (metaphorically speaking--what is this, the 90s?).

Best steak ever. We have been here three times in 5 months, enjoying each experience as much as the previous. This is our favorite restaurant in Austin. The chefs counter is a great experience to interact with staff while they prepare the foods, while also affording you the possibility of getting little tastes here and there of something you might not have ordered. The food quality, service, drink selection and overall quality of dining experience is top notch.
I love Ethiopian food and I LOVE this place! Super yummy vegetarian items, very polite staff and clean. This joint gets busy so arrive early on weekends, if you have a larger party.

The food here was good. It's not a must-do that I'd have to return to eat, but it sufficed for lunch. I acquired a same-day ADR on Columbus Day.  I'd originally had one ADR a day for our WDW trip, but we learned the hard way the obstacles of that is that, we're starving for the rest of the day until dinner time everyday. Plus the quick service options don't look that great. We were seated right away, and learned that walk-in waits took up to 40 minutes!This was a huge restaurant with seating on two floors. Disney really did a good job with decorating and creating the ambiance for this restaurant. It is located in Asia in Animal Kingdom, and the vibe this place gave off, was a lodge near Mount Everest. It matched with the decor and style of the area for the standby line on Expedition Everest (best ride I've ever experienced on Disney property!).  There were brown chairs of different styles, some ornately carved, some simple. Lots of browns and red for the color scheme. And in front of us was a huge figure with a bird mask. That was my favorite part of the restaurant.  The restaurant was also pretty loud because it was packed. The service was so so. She politely came by to take our order and bring us our food, but it took forever for her to come by when we wanted a refill or we wanted to get our check. Meh. Hubby and I wanted to be really hungry for dinner so we ordered the duck dish to share. We're not big people, so one dish usually suffices for us to eat.  When we got the dish, I thought it looked beautiful. The duck leg and thigh were a bright maroon color from the barbecue sauce. It was moist with crispy skin. The sauce was a tad too sweet though. It was served on a bed of rice, which I like because I can't live without that. There were some sauteed red peppers, carrots, mushrooms, onions and bokchoy. A bit soggy. They tasted like the frozen veggies you'd get at the store, and they only added bokchoy and fresh cilantro to make it more asian. Overall, this was a decent and filling dish, if not a bit pricey. Of course I say that in nearly all my reviews, especially if I don't think something was worth as much as how much I paid. Also, the straws here were pretty weird and made of paper, but I think they do that at AK so that if any animals came into contact with them, it wouldn't harm them. My experience here was okay. Decent food, a bit pricey, okay service. I'd like to try Tiffins or Tusker House instead, next time I return to Animal Kingdom.

I work in between downtown crossing and south station so vision care seemed like the best bet to get my prescription checked. I had been having issues in one eye and Dr. Zide suggested it was simply contact over wear. Low and behold after a week of less contact use my issue was resolved. Two month later I started to get some really bad migraine headaches along with some bad nausea. It all started with me wearing my glasses more often (which i got elsewhere during a groupon). Dr Zide looked at the glasses and discovered that my Pupil Distance was waaaay off which was causing my headaches while working on computers. Again, he was totally right and i've been wearing my glasses now at work without a headache for a full day. This is a huuuuge improvement and I owe it all to the great vision care team! I would highly recommend them!

looks like new management; lots of updates to the physical place: new paint, new salsa bar, new neon menu. But now the food sucks. They've got daily specials at great prices, but...crappy fish tacos are crappy fish tacos whether they're $.99 or $2.99. These were crap. Frozen spongy fish, way over salted, mealy yuckiness. My fav pickled carrots and onions were lame. They're charging for the housemade, super salty chips now as well. Too many taco shacks on BuHi to settle for this! NEXT!!!

Came in here my first night in Portland, and left me a good impression of how the rest of my trip may turn out. Beer is $4.50 (gladly cheaper than LA). Also have flights available. They have a wide variety on tap for you to choose from. Also have deals of beer and whiskey combos. Everyone was super friendly. Filled with communal seating inside and outside. There's also a nice fire pit outside to keep warm. Portland definitely has a thing (a good thing) for fire pits. For a Friday night it wasn't crowded. A very relaxed environment with good beer.
So impressed by the friendly staff and amazing food. I ordered the scallops and glad I did. Expect to wait on your food but you should anyway if you are going for fresh! Excellent excellent service!

The reviews on this cafe are all over the place.  I find it to be so-so and therefore I rarely go there.  The staff are usually friendly and efficient.The food is reasonably good but the biscuits are disappointintg.

Worst Cab company ever Will never call them againThe dispatcher lied by saying it will be there in 10 minutes. After an half wait I called again they said....it's been busy and will be there in a few minutes. 45 minutes later a third call and they said a few more minutes. At this point I gave up and called green cabs and they were at my door in 8 minutes.Why the Lies? I ask myself...and now  I say I will never ever call them again

My family and I went here for my birthday and had a wonderful experience. Our waiter was attentive and nice. The food was excellent and the portions were refreshingly reasonable. I got the gnocchi, which was delicious. Plenty of fresh, yummy veggies along with the potato pasta. The other entrees we ordered were the pork tenderloin and both specials, the herb-crusted salmon and the grass-fed beef tenderloin. All the meat and fish was cooked and seasoned perfectly and the presentation was beautiful.We ordered both the chocolate mousse cake and the spicy chocolate creme brulee for dessert. The creme brulee was better by far, served with a strawberry and mint. Sinfully delicious. The chocolate mousse cake doesn't have chocolate mousse in it, it's strawberry flavored mousse layered with choco cake. Good, but not nearly as impressive as the creme brulee. But they comped the cake for us, so I'm not complaining.Overall, a terrific experience. Thanks for a great birthday dinner!

Reasonably priced, tasty local joint. Lots of goodies you would see at the Flying Elephants downtown as well as the original Elephant's Deli. Beers for pretty cheap compared to a typical restaurant. Food is fresh. Probably one of the best places you can get non-airport food in an airport!

Dr Jackson , and her staff, have been wonderful.   I appreciate the time and concern they show towards patients.   Dr Jackson takes the time to explain, as do her techs and nurses.  I would highly recommend this practice

Same as my friend Jamie above.  I KNOW the food is good at Scoozis.  I am a fan, especially their panini's and pizza. But my last experience (service-wise) was just really dissappointing and left me and my party in a crappy mood.  Who wants to leave a restaurant in a bad mood?  But Katie was professional and respectful, and I appreciate/understand her concern.  Looking forward to going back and giving it another shot.  Thanks Katie.
Love the food and the price here.... But the waitress service was horrible that's why I give 3 star...

Love this place. I swear it feels like home. The food is cooked fresh so it take a little bit but not to long. The Embilta special is great to share. The owner is welcoming and always kind. I choose this spot over some of the more popular spots in Atlanta any day.

We ventured in here when the place we were going to eat lunch at was too packed but, I have wanted to try this place for a while!  The parking in this lot is a nightmare so, I would recommend parking at HEB and walking over.  The interior isn't anything to write home about; just your standard quick serve ambiance.It's like an assembly line of sandwiches or salads, much like subway!  Since it was our first time we didn't really know how it worked but we were on our own to figure it out as the employees didn't ask if we had dined with them before and then offer us an explanation.I ordered a Kebap with beef and lamb and then added a little lettuce, cucumber, onion and topped it with the garlic sauce.  It was nice that they put sauce on first and top it at the end again.  I think this is the only thing that saved my sandwich from being so dry that I threw it away.  That being said, I was very disappointed with the meat because I was thinking it would be juicy due to the cooking process and that lamb was in the combination.  It was very dry and not very flavorful.  The bread was decent but, coupled with the dry meat, it didn't help. The veggies were nice and fresh and that was a plus.  They do have a nice bottled beverage selection.I also sampled a French fry from my friends place and they were decently seasoned and fried well.Overall I was disappointed but, after speaking to some other yelpers I found out that they swear by some of the other locations.  Maybe I will venture to another location to try it again.

We stopped in to Padriac's late on a Monday because we wanted a bite and saw the Yelp deal on the handy Yelp app. $10 for $20 worth of goodies? Yeah, we can do that. Trivia had just ended, the Braves game was on (loudly), and we settled in to a gigantic booth. The waitress was super perky and greeted us and recited the specials for the evening. I was pleased to see they had Red Stripe Light for a mere $3: hooray! The menu is upscale bar food with nicer than normal options, like the tomato caprese salad I chose. It was fine, pretty much what you expect at a bar. My man's gouda tots looked, um, fried. A little bit of a hiccup when we went to use the Yelp deal. We had paid, waitress had taken our money, written down the code, and then came back and said we had to spend at least $30 to redeem it. What the what? There was absolutely nothing in the deal's terms and conditions that mentioned a minimum tab. We reluctantly ordered another round at the waitress' suggestion, as she said it'd cover it. Well, turns out we were still $3 short, and knowing I'd likely not be back here to use the deal at a later date, we paid for $3 worth of air. Awesome. I'm really leaning toward a 2 here due to the Deal issues, but I know that's not commonplace. Just be wary if you're planning on using one.

Love this place, the tacos are always on point. Plus with how busy they are, they always manage to Fer your food out quickly. The salsas are nice also. The staff is very friendly and laid back, great joint to go to if you want some good tacos.
Found Natasha via Yelp after she responded to an appointment request. She's very sweet and FAST!! She did a great job on my nails. I'll definitely be back.

Just as good as the last time I had it! Maybe even better?? :) The staff are friendly and professional, food is out of this world and the ambience is superb. I wish there was a Hopdoddy where I live!!

If you're in Cambridge and you need a sushi fix, Blue Fin is a great place to fill your craving.  This small, but reasonably priced, sushi spot offers a number of great rolls and nigri and other traditional Japanese dishes.  Even though there are bigger and flashier sushi spots in Boston, this one is well worth sampling.  You wont be disappointed.   Insiders note: try the garlic chicken.

Who can deny great seafood? No one. Summer Shack has some of the freshest seafood, directly from the fisherman in Boston. I had a 1-1/4 lb Lobster for $20 last night, and it was phenomenal.  Not only is the food great but so is the service. Awesome sports bar within the restaurant, with a projector and a pool table. They have five locations within greater Boston, so go to one near you!

Sorry this is a no from us. Four of us dined here earlier in the week. Three people couldn't even eat their meals they were that bad. The soup tasted just like a bowl of warm cinnamon, the creamy chicken pasta had so much blue cheese it was inedible. Spaghetti bolognese wasn't too bad. Drinks were good, Moscow mule not served in a copper cup (that's just being picky). Espresso martinis were good. The decor reminded me of the lobby of a holiday inn express. Server was in training but really good.

The only place I could get this cute BIRDIE CAKE in Boston area. Much better than the Tour Les Jours store in downtown Boston, I love the artistic decoration and the atmosphere here. Since the store are full of great tasting and good looking bakeries, the staffs are willing to help me choose the best cake and very patient with my indecision. I would also recommend matcha espresso. Thank Phillip for my beautiful drink .

First off I didn't even get to try the food.   I went into the restaurant and was met by a disgusting smell.  I stood there for several minutes and was not helped.  And most of the signage was not in English.   I Love all kinds of Asian food but these things added up to me walking out.   Just my experience.
The spicy Shrimp in the appetizer was packed with flavor, probably my favorite shrimp dish, but the bed of greens was out-of-the-bag salad with julienne cucumber, very pedestrian.

I ate here with my family on New Year's Eve (entering 2008) while visiting relatives in the area.  This particular Uno's seemed a bit small and cramped to me (with the usual long wait that happens around the dinner hours), but still had the usual classic decor that all the Uno's locations have.  Our waiter was very friendly and the salmon (along with the mashed potatoes and steamed broccoli that I always order as my sides) was wonderful.

I was super excited to try this place but ended up not liking it as much as I thought I would. I'm glad I can say I tried it though. The donuts were way too sweet and stale. The cashier was pretty rude and the place was so humid. This is not a place I'd recommend to anyone.
The best Thai food I have ever had. Everything was so delicious especially the taro fritters!

Good acts in a friendly local joint where it's too dark to care, or even notice, who's wearing/doing/saying what, etc.  A chill scene on Sunday when the jazz brunch dishes up solid food in generous portions along with mimosas and music.  Strange but true:  one afternoon, frustrated by the lack of seats & inter-table ogling at Diesel, Someday, and even Starbucks, I dragged my laptop and books over to Johnny D's where I sipped at a glass of wine and worked on my thesis in peace.  I highly recommend this.

Came here for a quick breakfast cum brunch before heading out to Stanley park. This place is located inside the Payal business center. Wow- I must say I am impressed by the number of Indian businesses here. It's a convenient place to do all of your Indian shopping without going anywhere else- clothes, grocery, sweets, snacks- you name it. We were immediately seated and our order was taken. We came here the next day as well. Too  convenient since it's one of the few places that opens at 10 am. On the first day we ordered tea, coffee, paav bhaji and chole bhature. I must say, we were not impressed by the taste of the food. Paav bhaaji was decent but it could have more of the masala to make it taste more like the authentic paav bhaaji. The chole lacked flavor. The coffee was too watery and the tea too milky. We came back next day just to save some time before heading back to Seattle. This time, we ordered one coffee, masala dosa and samosa chana. I wanted to get vada sambar but they were out of vada. The coffee was really good this time. Dosa was ok but the samosa chana was great. They have maintained the place really neatly. The girls working around the restaurant were cleanliness freaks in a good way. Overall a good reasonably priced place to have brunch in Surrey. Lots of parking available!

Do not have to pre-think about workout before arriving. Every workout is different. High intensity makes me feel like I am optimizing my 60 minutes. Music and energy of class makes the 60 minutes fly by. Its super fun and you see results!  Also, great coaches and staff!

The Harvard Coop and its counterpart the MIT Coop are overpriced. Buy your text books on amazon.com and your pencils from CVS or an art store. I suppose if you really have to have that Harvard sweatshirt or that MIT coffee mug you could make use of this store. It is conveniently located though and Harvard and MIT students can join to get some cash savings.BUT the Harvard Coop does have the best selection of academic books you will find anywhere in the area.  Looking for some theoretical mathbooks, yes they've got a good selection.  What about that computational linguistics blah blah, yep that too.And my personal favorite, the wall of architecture books and monographs.  Best selection in town, hands down.  But pricey.  Good for browsing, not for buying.

I didn't even know I liked Indian food until I went to Bukhara. Their food is amazing. I always order the veggie Korma or the cheese Korma, both mouth-wateringly good, I'm even getting hungry for them just sitting here writing about it. The prices are not bad, I don't remember exactly, but I think entrees are like $12 or so and you do get enough to have leftovers.

Ok so it seems others are complaining about the service, but my girlfriend and I thought it was good... Other than that it was a miserable experience.First we started with the calamari. Bland, even when dipped in the tasteless tomato sauce, and looked like they are from a cheap frozen bag.Next up, for my girlfriend, the fried fluke special with truffle mashed potatoes, beans, and salad. Again, the salad, beans, and surprisingly the mashed potatoes, were incredibly bland. The fluke was dry and had close to no flavor.For me, the salmon with spinach and bacon bits special. Spinach tasted like spinach but nothing special. The bacon, which is nearly impossible to make taste bad, sucked. The salmon had been cooked so long that skin on the bottom was burnt to the fish and couldn't be removed. Also, they topped it with a garnish of pickled fiddlehead ferns, which didn't mix well and was kind of gross.Altogether the price came out to $75, which is a hell of a lot for really crappy food.Overall? Never. Going. Back.
One of the better 24 hour pho places in the Burmaby area. Staff isn't too friendly but at least the food comes out fast. Good for groups.

We came here on our last day of our vacation. The decor is very nice inside and the staff is friendly. We tried the dim sum and overall about 8-10 dishes. The quality is good and authentic but a little on the pricey side. I would come back again.

If in Boulder and you're 'Yelpless', do the visual rating to choose the right dining spot.  Located in the main neighborhood shopping area of Boulder, we did our window cruising at 5:30 pm during 'happy hour' - most of the eateries were just waking up for the evening.  Dropped in on an interesting art gallery along our path and Ms. 'visual artistic person' in the gallery pointed us through the alleyway across the street and to the right to the most beautiful hotel lobby with 'very comfy sofas'.  St. Julien's Hotel with 1/2 price happy hour menu - very good pomme frites and excellent glasses of wine.  Oh, before we entered St. Julien's T-Zero Bar we were given 40 minute wait for two at Brasserie Ten Ten directly across the street from St. Julien's.  Ok, a little sidetracked here.  We decided on BTT because at 5:45pm the place was PACKED!Reminiscent of European restaurants the menu has an excellent variety with a daily prix fixe to boot.  This evening the fixed featured a goat cheese salad, braised oxtail and capping off with a sharable bread pudding.  My choice was a simple salad and a wonderful bouillabaisse with the best thin broth - more bread needed please.Service was outstanding and extremely efficient - zero complaints.So, when Yelpless, go for the window cruise method and find the most crowded spot early.Got out for less than $70 including two glasses of good wine!
Things are fresh and good here. The menu is a checklist and the wines are admirable.

We arrived and were seated promptly. Ordered a Bloody Mary, eh. Our food arrived within fifteen minutes, pretty impressed and it was delicious. I ordered the Belgian waffles with the green tomato syrup on the side and bacon. Omg it was so good! My bf ordered the brisket hash and a side of sausage. Again really tasty. Only complaint is they took food to box up and never brought it back :(

1. No one greeted us at door. We waited 5 minutes , while their staff ignored us.2. They sat us down on a table for 1. Meanwhile, a selfish woman was sitting at a table for 4 sipping her coffee and reading a magazine like it's a coffee shop.3. Waited another 20 minutes and nothing. Others were getting helped, while we were completely ignored.This was my first time here and I eat out a lot. You can count on never seeing me, my wife, and our friends here again

Ate at this delightful, hipster restaurant recently and will be going back soon. It was delicious and by far one of the best meals I've eaten for brunch. I started off with a delicious, chocolate, mocha chino . Then shared the avocado toast which was spectacularly delicious. Avocado was fresh and not over riped-perfect. For my meal, I had the Le Complet. Flat iron steak was seared to a tender, juicy, flavorful, medium-rare perfection.my over easy eggs, perfectly paired with the steak brought harmony to my taste buds. The tomato, basil toast and sauce brought a delicious finish to a wonderful meal. My mom, had the fricasse, which I got to try. The short ribs, so tender they fell off the bone and melted in your mouth. My hubby had the wolfs platter, where he sampled perfectly cooked sausage, pork belly bacon, and over-easy eggs. He was in men's, meat nirvana. For dessert we had the delicious waffles with mixed berry sauce.Waitress was very friendly, attentive, and informative on recommending meals, since this was our first time eating here. She was very helpful and gave us great suggestions, always refilled our coffee and never left us unattended. Ambience was hipster, and crowded. We only had to wait a few minutes for a table, but it was well worth the wait. We enjoyed waffles so much, that we took some to go. We enjoyed the mango and dark chocolate sauce. Can't wait to go back and enjoy my new favorite place in Vancouver.

Great place for lunch!  Thai Cuisine has an all you can eat appetizer / salad bar that is included with lunch and makes this place a great deal.  It is always stocked with salad, spring rolls, some kind of dessert, two soups, and 2 different fried specialties. For the main course, I really like the curry specials, the spicy cashew chicken, and the basil fried rice.  Lines during the week can be long though, so it is best to go when you are eating early or late.  Arriving M-F between 12-12:45 usually means a wait of ~20 minutes or so.

We moved into our house 2 years ago and I emailed 3 companies to ask for a consult just to see how healthy our trees were. Capitol Tree Care replied to our request very quickly and we were able to schedule a visit at our convenience. James arrived on time and was friendly, professional and knowledgeable; answered all our questions and gave us some great info on where we could improve the health of our tress and what we could leave alone. Zero pressure for additional work- we then asked for a quote which was then emailed to us before he left the driveway. Will definitely stay with this company for future work and would highly recommend to others.
Some of the nicest vets you'll ever met. They offer 24 hour emergency services (you have to call ahead), grooming, and ever run an animal shelter. I don't trust my pets to anyone else.
Lily did my nails and pedicure she is amazing. I will recommend anyone to come here. The service is awesome and the energy in this place is peaceful.

Ride is the best spin studio in Austin.  Friendly staff and a clean studio but the real standout which makes this place so special is the team of instructors that make every single class exciting, challenging and they always show up with 100% energy.  Every instructor I've tried has been phenomenal so you can't go wrong. Expect an intense butt kicking workout.  Your first class is free so try it out but be warned, once you try it, you will get addicted.

Absolutely Excellent! I never in my life thought I would try Ethiopian food but it has turned out to be one of my all time favorite cuisines due to all the amazing food I have had at Desta. My wife loves the vegetable platter, but I gotta have meat to call it a meal so I went with the ribeye tibs the first time around, and my second and third visit the filet mignon tibs. Filet mignon just less fatty and more tender, but both were excellent! The wait staff are attentive and friendly and it makes for a great evening. HIGHLY RECOMMEND this place to anyone!

This is, unfortunately, my Safeway.  I live so close it would be dumb for me to not shop there.  However, after multiple disgusting experiences, its worth the walk down to Whole Foods in the Pearl.The constant presence of beggars on the corners really becomes exhausting after awhile.  There is a smell in the store that at times has made me gag.  And, I have worked in the operating room and ER environment for 11 years.  That is saying something.I purchased Parmesan cheese, and when I went to actually use it, that same day, I noticed it had expired 3 months ago.  Now, if I was at my grandmother's, who used to keep Cheerios that were so old there were little black bugs in it (sweetie,,,its fiber,,,,No Grandma,,,,those are bugs,,,,well sweetie,,,if you chew it quick and swallow, you won't taste them,,,,and yes,,,she was still talking about the cereal).  Customer Service would not exchange my Parmesan Cheese.  The selection for a lot of items are limited.  The staff is rarely friendly (although there is an older checker who is always super pleasant).  The check out lines are always ridiculous. The Starbucks inside is heaven for a new psychologist who is anxious to save the world.  They now have a gluten free section.  Too bad its unreasonably expensive.  I cannot wait for another competing market to open in this area, because they would get a lot of business.

The fried braised brisket empanadas are really good. The filling is a little sweet and reminds me a bit like the Chinese Char Siu Pau. The fried sweet corn empanadas are pretty good as well. Subtly sweet, thick and creamy filling.The glazed pork cheeks came in 3 pieces glazed in Malbec caramelized sugar and vinegar. The duck breast is probably my #1 favorite. Perfectly cooked, soft and slightly red.

Overpriced restaurant and poor service. The lobster bun costs $16 which is way over priced. The soda comes with half glass of big ice cubics. I know the rent could be expensive near the mall, but seven lamps is ridiculously pricy compared to other restaurants in Lenox.

My husband and I got married at this perfect place on June 15, 2014.  Michelle and the entire staff treated us with the upmost respect, were highly organized, friendly and attentive.  Our 88 guests and my husband and I had a perfect wedding.  The food was superb, the decorations, the grounds, the service reception, music and time of events were done perfectly.  We were so happy to have the perfect day, because we did not have to worry about anything.  I will recommend the Hampshire House to any one who wants to have a perfect, well organized, Bostonian wedding in the heart of the Boston Public Gardens.  Loved, loved, loved our wedding day!

Delightful dining experience!  Visited Besito Sunday night with a large group.  No one was disappointed.  Food was delicious, spinach, plantain and roasted corn sides very tasty; tortilla soup divine, apps very well done, particularly table side guacamole (everyone loved it), entrees delicious and dessert outstanding!  Would return in a heart beat.  Atmosphere beautiful and service top notch. Congrats to all at Besito!

Wanted to try authentic Italian food, and was unimpressed. The place looked nice with a phantom gourmet sticker and so I was expecting food that was decent. The meatballs and spaghetti I got tasted like tomato mixed with water. I don't know what authentic Italian food is supposed to taste like but Olive Garden or Mall good shouldn't taste better. I might give it another shot one day, but I guess I'll see.

Not a problem here. I was only getting some gift cards. I love purchasing Chipotle cards for people to turn them onto the food fresh food served here. They have the most amazingly fresh housemade guacamole. Oh occasion when standing at the register I have watched them make it in the kitchen. Again, I was only getting gift cards but I observed the following. The store as usual was packed. The line was long and they had a good amount of help. This is actually a good thing. Employees seemed polite to the customer from what I could hear. Many people were dining in. The drink area looked very clean and it might have been since I did see an employee cleaning off the tables. I walked up to the register and was greeted right away. Although the young girl was helping someone complete their order I was still greet right away. The employee was very polite to me and helpful. I would for sure be back again, this time for food. The only reason not 5 stars was because I did not purchase food, which I am quite sure I will give them that 5 stars rating once I have tried the food.

I've had brunch and dinner there in the past week. It's great! The food is wonderful and full of flavour. Every dish was spot on. The ambiance is very relaxed and in the summer they open up to let in a lot of fresh air. Prices are reasonable for the high quality food.My only complaint is that on Mondays they seem to have a trivia night in the restaurant. This is really awkward and noisy. It doesn't fit the place at all.Hops and Pilgrim are the best dinner you can get in the area and Hops is quite a bit better value. Go there!

I read a review somewhere saying that the cocktails at this hotel were amazing! So during my week long vacay in ATL I had to check it out! The location of this hotel is ri downtown adjacent to the ferris wheel! Parking is super shady, and in 4 inch knee high boots I glady paid the $15 for parking. The ambience of the bar is minimal. Theres serveral couches, tables, and seats at the bar. We opted to sit at a couch. There appears to be a fire pit and outside seating area.  However, I never checked it out. At first with the parking and typical hotel scenery I wasnt impressed..Until I drank my cocktail. We ordered their spin on an old fashion... and it was worth everything! The Bartender was phenom! The drinks were perfect!
Simply put - Hands down the BEST gyro I have ever eaten!  I highly recommend this place for tasty Mediterranean food.  You won't be disappointed.

I called on Monday to have some old decking planks hauled away.  Chad was just as nice and friendly as he could be and put us on the schedule for the next day.  They arrived with truck, trailer and chainsaws in hand and were done in a blink of an eye.  They even swept up the small debris and we could not be happier with their service.  Folks, believe me, this is what customer service is all about.  Great job Chad and Kevin, great job!

This is as if all breakers houses were combined. Their buttermilk pancakes were something I couldn't stop eating, my bacon was perfectly made crispy as I like them, the sausages were perfect and juicy and my almost favorite part (the pancakes were) was the orange juice which in the menu says was freshly squeezed and it tasted as if I was just eating an orange which is great. My last comment is their service. They weren't fake people saying it's a great day every day they seemed actually happy to do their job and that's what I love.

I have eaten several meals here.   Both lunch and dinner.  It is much better value at lunch time.  One of my favorites is the miso Cod.  The desert trio is also excellent.For lunch or a late dinner it is usually fairly quiet.  If you are there around happy hour it can be quit noisy.

This was our first hot pot experience in Boston.  After reading the reviews from Yelp, I was excited.  The reviews were spot on this time.  We were seated upstairs on a Sunday afternoon.  The place was pretty much empty.  We ordered  the Japanese curry and kimchi curry base, with a vegetable plate and a lamb/chicken plate.  Overall, a great place to check out on a cold winter day for some flavorful soup.  Prices were decent and the concept of creating your own soup was fun!!

The donuts here are excellent. However, I can't say that they are my favorite donut shop considering the price. If you want a bakers dozen, expect to pay over 30 bucks easily. Considering the number of other quality delicious donut shops in the area that are much less, I can't give this spot my complete approval. You will not be disappointed by the donuts, but you will probably get a bit of a sticker shock on your first visit.However, the space is clean and neat. The donuts change constantly. The flavors are unique. The service is excellent. If you want a cool donut experience, check these guys out. However, its a bit too pricey to be a regular stop.

I'm brand new to the area so I thought I'd run over the nearest mexican place I could find.I was greeted by two extremely friendly owners (granted I was the only one in the place ~12pm). After a quick chat, they recommended I get the tacos and a tamale. I got a carne asada taco and a green chili pork taco. I told them to do it how they usually prepare them which was with beans, cheese, lettuce, pico, and cilantro. They ran me through the salsas they had available and I went with one hot and one mild salsa. 5-7 minutes and $10 and I was out with my to-go order (it was a combo so it included chips and a drink).Got home and opened things up. Had the carne asada taco first. It was good. Not great, not mind blowing, but it was good. Next up was the tamale. It was both great and mind blowing. Highly recommend getting the tamale... I had the pork with red chili and it was fantastic. The right amount of seasoning, served in the husk- it was just as good as my friend's mom used to make. Saved the green chili taco for last, and it was like the first taco- pretty good.I mixed in salsas with the meal during the process and their salsas are fantastic. Combine with tamale = near to mexican heaven.I fully understand the limitations on quick, relatively cheap, and casual mexican dining, so my experience was awesome. Next time I go, I'll probably be going with the burrito or quesadilla to potentially keep things together better/get more flavors in there. I'll definitely be getting those tamales every chance I get.The reason I docked them a star is because the hours are kind of selective, so it'll be harder to go here with people, and they don't have a liquor license (or byob policy) to serve beer/margaritas, yet.

If you've never had the pleasure of experiencing Korean food- this is the only game in town. A welcome addition to Boston. The food is delightfully light and fresh. Try the Ba Bim Bap for two which arrives at your table in a sizzling stone bowl. You stir it up and gobble it up. Great place for a romantic evening for foodies or groups. Dig in! Meat lover or Veg alike will agree it's simply delicious.

What happened!!??   Where did the sandwich & salad combo go?  My favorite lunch item was removed from the menu!   I loved (past tense) to go their with my work friends to have lunch.  I would get 1/2 steak sandwich (or other sandwich) and this wonderful salad they had, but now - it is gone.  I don't know that I am going back here again.  It was reasonable and delicious.  Now it is gone!

After strolling thru Public Garden and Beacon Hill mid afternoon, I was looking for a place to pop in and have a cold beer and some lunch. Quick search of the area on Yelp brought me to The Sevens Ale House. I walked in around 12:45 or so on a beautiful fall Thursday and the place was empty but for one other costumer dining in the corner. I thought about abandoning my plan but was then greeted by John, one of the staff there, and decided to give it a go anyhow. I sat at the bar and quickly asked for and was given a Sam Adams Oktoberfest draft and the menu. I went with the Pulled Pork sandwich with a side of potato chips, and it hit the spot! Really tasty pulled pork on a slight toasted roll was exactly what I was wanting--and the beer was perfect for washing it all down with! After finishing my food, I ordered a second beer to enjoy and lingered for a bit longer. Had some nice friendly conversation again with John working there and slowly more people trickled in. Of all of those that had entered from when I first sat down (maybe 10 or so?) all appeared to be local/regulars as they knew/were known by everyone there. It gave the impression/vibe of a great local hangout. All and all it was a pleasant experience and a great joint for a nice and simple bite to eat and cold fresh beer. Recommended.
Loved it. Party of three tried different burgers and really liked all three. Great onion rings good sweet potato tater tots. Nacho sat by us and was very friendly. Glad we took the ferry from Boston.
Solid middle of the road chain, I had the fish tacos which were pretty good. The rice and beans as a side were better than expected.

Whenever we travel, we make it a point to ask a local (usually a police officer, since who knows the area better?) where the best 'local' place is to eat. In this case, I AM the local and this is my choice for best local 'flavor'. First of all, when I walk in I feel like they should be playing the theme from 'Cheers' and Norm should be sitting at the bar. For the local residents, you just know that you are going to run into someone you know and for the not so local it's very easy to get caught up in the jovial camraderie that flows through the restaurant. The waitstaff is cordial and busy but never hurried...you can spend as much or as little time dining as you wish. The food is flavorful, plentiful, and inexpensive, which is a tough combination to beat. The Colonial House is located on a side street in a residential neighborhood with no sign announcing its presence. In spite of this, the Colonial House is always packed with happy diners. My choice for the best 'local flavor' in Norwood is The Colonial House on Savin Avenue.

This is a pretty decent Five Guys, as far as Five Guys go. The staff is friendly, the food is just as fast (or slow...) as other Five Guys locations I've been to, and the food is fresh. I find Five Guys to be a bit overpriced, but that's not the fault of this location.Good parking, near a lot of other things... so, overall this place is a-okay!

Molana has one of the most tender Chicken Bargs I have ever had in my life! (and I have had alot of them) So delicious,  beautifully seasoned,  and super tender. We also got the Koubideh, that was also well seasoned, was cooked well, and was still juicy and tender. And last, but not least, the Ghorme Sabzi was so great. The strew could use a little more beans, but it was so well-cooked and tasted like those you'd have at your mom's or auntie's house Keep up the great work, Molana!

At first I was skeptical. But I was convinced to go for their great special of a pizza and 2 beers for $10. What a deal! We ordered the supreme pizza and it was delicious! The toppings tasted extremely fresh and having a nice cold beer to wash it down was just the finishing touch. The crust was also super delicious too, put a little Parmesan on it and it taste similar to the home slice garlic knots. Definitely going back!

Unless the chef is fired soon, this place has no chance of survival in the next six months.The waiter, Leonard, was great. I also liked the kitschy interior.The food was  bland. Some items weren't even fresh. The first thing we were served was cold HEB sliced italian bread. If you are not going to bake your bread, then get some interesting bread and warm it up. This is one of the worst bread experiences I've had at a restaurant. I would recommend not even serving bread. We got the house specialties at 20 bucks per entree. The owner needs to go to Vespaio or  Asti's and see that you can get food, which is ten times better for a few bucks more. I'm not trying to be cruel but the marinara at Olive Garden and Macaroni Grill is so much better. I would have rather eaten at either of these two places. I actually think Macaroni grill is pretty good. Verona's is not even half as good. Really disappointing food that does not turn around quickly because of few clients. There was old iceberg in my salad. The crab cannelloni had not been prepped correctly and included fibrous parts of the artichoke.  I hope the restaurant that replaces this in the near future is better.

The Black Bear Diner is like Denny's but with character and great food. The menu is big, the portions are bigger, they serve breakfast all day and everyone in my family of 4 were happy with their meals.

An ok place, staff are friendly but we were placed in an area that our server had with 2 large parties. Food came out at best warm and had to be sent back. Looks nice in presentation, fair in taste and a bit too salty.

Absolutely the best Chinese food around. Not heavy with grease like many Chinese restaurants. The staff is amazing. When you dine it they treat you like you're in a formal restaurant (casual attire is the way). They also deliver! We have had delivery a dozen times at least and our order has always been accurate and arrived hot and fast! I can't say enough wonderful things about this place. My only regret is that we didn't find it sooner. Living in the neighborhood it took us several years to try the spot because of location and the name; golden rule...don't judge a book by its cover. You won't be disappointed.

It's hard to believe that this is a restaurant in an airport. Grouped among the Subway's and Arby's of the world this is a secret gem in Terminal E. The Soy Glazed Grouper was out of this world. They give you a very bountiful portion of fish on top of fresh okra and bok choy in a marvelous soy flavored sauce. The wait staff was extremely friendly and attentive. The first thing they do when you sit down is to ask how long you have to ensure you have enough time to enjoy your meal or put a rush on orders in the kitchen to guarantee you make your flight.
Its awesome to have a super hero store...  Its like entering into The Shield.  The reason I gave it only three stars is because its such a tiny store...  It gets packed quickly and warm inside.

Two successful visits and will certainly be hitting up this place for lunch pretty regularly. A great addition to the Decatur scene. The empanadas at five bucks for two with some greens is a great buy, and adding a side for two more bucks gives you probably the most economical filling meal in town. The arepas are fine, too.
Place has a trendy atmosphere and food is okay but nothing special. Will probably comeback

I can't say enough good things about this hotel, and their amazing staff. I showed up virtually in the middle of the night, after having been turned away by a hotel which I had booked in advance. As a solo, exhausted, female traveler, I just needed somewhere inexpensive to rest my head. I walked into the Hampton inn obviously exhausted and Jeff did the most amazing thing. He called EVERY hotel nearby and asked if they had an open room and what the price was. He was trying to get me the best deal, but of course everything was booked. Then feeling bad for this crazy girl he gave me a hefty discount, and an amazing huge room with a massive King bed. So Jeff, thanks for being awesome, good karma is coming for you! 10/10 would stay again!

I can't say enough good things about Blue Ox. The oysters are some of the cleanest oysters I've ever eaten, the service is impeccable (total team effort to ensure you enjoy a great night), and the atmosphere (music, ambience, art-work, lighting) is spot-on. We love the local brew on tap (go Bent Water Brewing!) and the craft drinks are tasty. The food never disappoints and dessert should not be skipped. Sticky Toffee Pudding is an easy favorite. Just writing this review makes me want to go back for happy hour oysters tomorrow.
Great steak.  Really enjoyed the meal and the evening.  Very top cut steak and service comparable with high-end steakhouses.  Quaint location.

I live in Orlando and I heard about the opening of this new restaurant in the Millenia Mall; I wanted to come here so bad since my husband and I are foodies but we hadn't had a chance.My parents are visiting for the weekend and my mom is a sucker for The Cheesecake Factory.... we were actually heading that way when I thought of Earls and told them to give it a try... in hopes that it wouldn't disappoint us.We got here for a little after lunch time, maybe close to 3.00pm, and it was empty for a new restaurant, but it could have been the day and the hour. They offer valet for $7.00, and even if you don't make use of it -which we didn't-, the valet guys were such gentlemen they opened the door for us. We were greeted by two young ladies very excited about our first visit and the girl who sat us told us about the restaurant's concept and the art and decorations, including a full wall art made with Sharpie.The restaurant from my first impression can be described as: Elegant and Upscale. The servers are wearing formal attires and most of the lady servers are in heals (don't really know how they do it). Very clean space and incredible and unique decoration (different colors, tables, lightning, and art).Our server's name was Brooke S, and she was such a sweetheart. She explained that Earls was a Canadian food chain and that the concept was variety... and sure thing you open the menu and you get anything from Japanese to Vietnamese, Indian, American, and more. Prices are decent for the portions you get. One thing I loved was that she brought waters before anything else. That's a great touch, not everybody does it and you always need some water.We order the Tuna Poke with Wonton chips and the Garlic Fries as appetizers... that Tuna Poke IS A MUST! What a delicious twist to a poke! And the wonton chips.... oh my Lord! The fries were good but nothing to rave about.Then we proceeded to order a Chicken Caesar salad, the Half Rack of Ribs with the Cajun Chicken combo that came with potato salad and Cole slaw, and the Chicken Curry.Everything was amazing, from presentation, smells, and taste. I was even impressed with the caesar salad since it's so basic, I wasn't expecting it to be so good. The ribs were falling of the bone, that potato salad was fresh and crisp, and the curry... simply amazing! It came with jasmine rice and naan bread. It was spicy enough but no overpowering.Of course... at the end of our meal we couldn't pass on the sweet tooth, and we fell for the coconut cake. That one was a little disappointing, I didn't think the coconut was well paired with a lime mousse and strawberries, but it might be just me.At checkout time, the server brought the POS over to us since they don't take the credit card from you and you do the tip and confirm total yourself in front of the server. I know this is a new thing as of 2017 restaurants are not supposed to handle customer credit cards, so it was nice to see it in action.I loved to see the teamwork in this place. We knew who our server was but anybody who walked by us would take dirty plates of the way, ask about out experience, and bring water to the table. All of this being said... we're definitely coming back for more and to try the beverages selection which seems unique and exquisite.

I just signed up for the monthly unlimited express wash. I like to wash my own car but this winter is rough enough to interrupt life. At 35 bucks a month when it's 20 bucks regularly, I think the price is right. Other than the fact that brushes are used I like this car wash. Wheels and tires comes out nice and shiny. All in all it's a good wash.The negative is the towel dryers. I don't know how their tip jar fills up. They don't even wipe down the whole car, which ends up leaving streaks when you have driven for for a while. This really downgrades the wash. The second time I went through ( which was the next day) I brought my own microfiber towels an pulled over near ocean state job lot and dried my car. It produced a much more desirable outcome. That's another negative. As of right now there is no space on Waves property to further detail my car

Grew up on the meatball grinders and green pepper and onion pizza from this place, since back when a small sub was $2.37 with tax.  If I could get them to deliver to San Francisco, I'd be all set.  Sigh, it's SOOO all about the burrito here.It's like a comfort food for me -- if I go visit my family, I try to make a stop there.

We came on a Saturday night and were surprised that it was almost completely empty. We were a little worried because the only other table there left unsatisfied, but we ended up really enjoying ourselves.The portions, though not very large, were filling and all had strong flavors. Some dishes were a little too salty and though we all ordered medium spiciness level, our dishes ranged from extremely mild to very spicy. However, the naan was great, especially the garlic naan. I also really enjoyed that Punjabi did not skimp on ingredients. The lamb Rogan Josh had a good amount of lamb, and the Malai Kofta had four vegetable balls, while a lot of other places usually only have three. The service was courteous, though it was pretty clear that English wasn't their first language, which led to some confusion. They were super nice about splitting the check and were attentive with water refills.I think this place has a lot of potential. Honestly, I like it more than Diva down the street because their flavors are excellent though a little inconsistent . I'll definitely be coming back to see how this restaurant grows.

Had I reviewed Shi Chi a week ago, they might have gotten 3 stars. However, after my experience this weekend, they were fully downgraded.My husband and I decided to go there on Saturday night, thinking that we typically sit down easily there. Knowing it was Valentine's Day weekend, we called ahead and made resevations for 6:30pm for 2 people.We arrived a couple minutes after 6:30 and were told it would be about 10 minutes. Our thinking was 'no big deal, it's busy.' Well, 35 minutes and a complaining stop to the host stand later, we were finally seated. Then, we waited nearly 15 minutes to see a waitress. We considered leaving multuple times, but knew we'd have to wait all over again somewhere else. We stayed and were finally greeted by our chef. The food was ok- about what you'd expect from a Japanese steak house. The hibachi dinners start with soup (broth with a few green onions and pieces of tofu) and salad (with ginger dressing and bacon bits). You also get a few pieces of shrimp appetizer, hibachi vegetables and rice (I always get the fried rice). I got the kobe (steak) and chicken, while my husband got steak and lobster with a thick, creamy sauce. The best part is that dessert is included. You get your choice of vanilla ice cream or pineapple sherbert. Delicious way to end the meal!I have been there a handful of times before and had good experiences, but this one was pretty awful. I doubt we'll be back anytime soon.

The interior is great here. It was nice inside, had some unique decor with the mirror walls and lighting above as well as a nice big bar area with great comfy chairs, perfect for meeting a group for some drinks or an after meal drink. Food though, eh was kind of blah when it came to main courses. Drinks were good though - especially that Big Kahuna!We had a party of 5 so had a few different food options we got. The food was a bit pricey but some items that were just simple meals, nothing note worthy. We had a few people get the Korean Rubbed Sirloin. For the price you'd expect a pretty spot on delicious meat. But everyone agreed, it was SUPER bland! And some areas were so undercooked it was pretty much medium rare. For $43 you'd expect a juicy and flavorful meat but that dish left everyone  unimpressed. We also had the chicken wings (which were fabulous) and the Sa-Cha chicken stir fry. The stir fry as well was really bland! I was shocked because it had potential to have great flavor but again, was just not that fantastic. We did get a few appetizers which were good, which was the chicken teriyaki (which they should make into a main dish) and that was great. Also the lobster and crab rangoons were great. We felt like the appetizers were the way to go compared to the main dishes.Might try it again for the unlimited sushi as we heard good things. But for the $350 bill, definitely expected better.

Very clean, super fresh, really good food. Owner's philosophy is that it's like a food stand in Vietnam: everything is made fresh. Small place, counter seating, plus a few tables, some tables outside. Sampled 3 soups since they were out of bread for banh mi (complimentary spring rolls more than made up for that). Crab, pork meatball (my favorite, very delicate), and congee. Also tried the green dessert item with taro in it -- good!Will definitely be back. Very friendly owner, clearly hardworking and cares deeply about what he's doing. Not easy to spot -- look for the strip mall with green signs, flanked by Domino's.

I just bought my new 64 gig IPhone 6 on the new edge plan for $173 & no longer have a contract since that is slowly becoming antiquated with Verizon & all phone companies & my bill remains the same & now when I go to Vietnam & Hong Kong at the end of the month I will have so much storage for pictures & video & the actual quality is superb! I loved the IPhone 5 for the  2 1/2 years I had it but this is my summer for new adventures, experiences, & new toys!!I have never received such amazing customer service at a Verizon store in the 10+ years I have been with them even though it's always been good, by far the sales associate, Michael blew anyone & everyone out of the water with his superb knowledge & advice. He is also incredibly personable & as he backed up my old phone so he can get my new phone ready to go, we had an awesome conversation about traveling & various things. I'm extremely pleased with my choice to come to this new location & purchase my new phone today. If you're thinking about purchasing a new phone or need anything at Verizon, without hesitation I highly recommend this specific store!!! I'm so excited!! I love my new phone & can't wait to take pictures with my new phone!!! A+++ service all around. Everyone in the store was so friendly & personable & you will assuredly get exactly what you need with no hassle & excellent service!!!

She was a sweetheart and very willing to know about any medical history.  If you are looking for a luxurious place, this is not the place for you.  It's a small room in a building.  She was very respectful and soft spoken.   As for the massage, if you don't like strong strokes, then she's perfect.  But if you like strong massages, she may not be the person to go see.  I favor more the stronger massage more since I have stress related tension that needs strong hands. The place needed to be a little bit cleaner. Someone needs to help her with the up keep.   As for me, I will continue to seek a person with a little stronger hand, but for others; she just maybe just right.

Marta sucks compared to just about every other citys transit. Make sure you leave very early if you need to be somewhere on time! Not very safe either. Does the job, but way to exspensive for this kind of service.
We were seated in 10 minutes. Then no one took our order no one even asked us what we wanted to drink and they aren't even that busy. TERRIBLE SERVICE!

Thank you to Scrubadub for making my white Audi Q5 look amazing again. My car sustained copper/rust stains from a leaking garage pipe but Bruno and Linares buffed it out completely.  Thought I would need a new paint job but these took care of it in less than 3 hours. They also took care of the inside, which looks awesome now.

Eh... honestly? I think maybe you Portlanders have never had good donuts. If you are looking for a donut that's unique, eat at Blue Star but if you're looking for a great tasting donut, maybe eat somewhere else. If I'm gonna eat a 5 dollar donut (okay, $4.75), it better be amazing. But if I can get a more typical donut for a buck fifty that tastes way better... Then we have a problem.My wife and I had the raspberry glaze, the lemon poppyseed and the chocolate crunch. In fairness, the chocolate crunch was actually pretty good but the chocolate was a little bitter for me. But that's me. However the other two were both really dry. I will say the service was really good and they played great music. But after all the hype... and cost... Eh. I'm gonna go back to my apple fritter.

Had Thanksgiving dinner here - they were cranking out turkey plates, but I had a really lovely Caesar-ish salad and a vegetarian stuffed delicata squash with braised endive. The squash had wild rice, chanterelle mushrooms, dried apricots and cherries, and was tasty - I think they precooked it so it was actually tender enough you could eat it. The stuffing probably could've used another element other than the rice, but the fruit played really well with the mushrooms and sweet squash. The best thing I ate, however, was the lemony braised endive, which was easily one of ten most delicious things I have ever eaten. Pecan pie for dessert was very well executed, and service was attentive without being annoying - the runner was very charming. It's a noisy place...you can hear, but it's not a place for intimate conversations. Worth the prices and I'll definitely go back again for a special occasion meal, especially now that Genoa's gone. Interesting selection of cocktails and decent wines.

Meh. I want so badly to add another star. I actually love the low-key market environment with tubs of prepared salads and spreads and a deli counter, it's my absolute favorite way to lunch. But the chicken shwarma wrap was just bland. It was definitely fresh enough, but I just couldn't get any flavor from the chicken, it was like eating a tube of straight tahini.I will be back to try something else on recommendation from everyone I know who raves about this place.

This was probably my favorite place by far for food and entertainment! Way to loud for a place to go if you are meeting someone to chat but well worth the noise! There is a live DJ and the dancers are amazing movers/dancers, the napkins they throw everywhere is awesome, and the way they all encourage you to get up on your table or on the floor to dance and yell OPA. You do shots from standing on your chair and the servers are very attentive, fast with everything. Great food as well if you like authentic Greek food.
Very nice beer. Great environment . Nice people. They have different beers from evwrywhere. The environment is very joyful and fun. It is a great place to go and relax
This place was amazing. Casual dining featuring fresh food, great drinks, fun atmosphere with very nice servers.  I can't wait to come back!

This review is an update to the others, which are AT LEAST a year old.   * The cost is now $9.99 for dinner.   * Their bottled beer prices now top out at $1.99 (imports, including Asian), with domestics at $1.79.  * The mussels are good because they're not encased in cheese.   * The steamed salmon is better than at most buffets.   * Some of the meat combination dishes can be too salty for some people's taste.   * The service is good & not very intrusive.   * The desserts don't look very appetizing, but this is fairly common to Oriental buffets, for some reason. But, the ice cream is one of those vanilla/chocolate /swirl deals,  and there's a decent selection of toppings. OK...so that warrants 3 stars on my grading scale.This is a significant improvement over 2011 & 2012. And, it's about the same as most Oriental buffets. So, check it out for yourself!

The only think I have to say about Ha VL is that it definitely deserves 5 stars. Don't expect anything more than a tiny restaurant with old metal tables and shared seating. Only expect the two soups or short Bahn mi menu to be exceptional every time. I faithfully eat the Turmeric soup every Sunday....

I really cant say anything bad about this place. Be prepared to wait in line if you are going at a peak time but I promise that they keep the line moving! I sat at the bar - the service was amazing!! I had the Llano Poblano w/ caramelized onions and it was fantastic. I also had the truffle fries, a mini margarita (called a little Larry and it was strongggg, lol) and a Lonestar. My tab came to $25 so it's very reasonably prices. I'd absolutely come back the next time I am in town.
Wow. Stunning. Accommodating. Romantic. Modern. As close to perfect as you can get. No amateur review could do Juniper justice. Thank you!

Had a rare great experience here last night. We brought our Toyota in for a routine service appointment and were a bit late due to terrible traffic. They were able to fit us in, even though they were closing within an hour, and even washed our car. The service guy (I'm blanking on a proper job title), Ezra, was wonderful and gave us a discount. The manager came over to say hello and was very kind. We were even invited to partake in a catered dinner they were having for new Toyota customers.

I went in for an 80 minute prenatal massage.. I had really been looking forward to it because I've had a lot of stressful things going on and just wanted to decompress and get a couple spots worked on that have been bothering me. The front staff was great while I was there. However this is based off of my experience during massage. In my 80 minute massage the massage therapist talked 99% of the time (not even an exaggeration), and even though she worked on my back as requested, she did not work on my specific spots near my shoulder blades that I verbally told her had been bothering me (twice). I've (now) had two masssages ever so this was a big deal to me to spend that much money on one. To be honest when I left I cried in my car because this was not relaxing to me AT ALL when she literally talked just about the entire time. On top of that  my boyfriend had spent $60 on the gift certificate + I paid another $60 after I got there for a service that I wasn't happy with. I'm still having issues with the areas by my shoulder blades and to be honest don't feel any different from prior to having the massage (unlike my first one where I felt a lot of relief / this was done at a different business out of the area with my last pregnancy). I left feeling more stressed out than when I went in for the massage. If I go back, it would not be to this location. I wish I had read the yelp reviews prior to scheduling here. Disappointed is an understatement.

It's hard not to have great things to say about the bar within walking distance of your inhabitants. It is a shame that I have not visited in my time living in Atlanta until now. It has a great neighborhood vibe.I loveeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeed (that's a lot of love) the Sweet Potato Appetizer. It was super delicious. Bite sized sweet potato bites glazed with a small amount of buffalo sauce and a creamy garlicky sauce. YUM YUM YUM... I also had the pleasure of eating the Arugula Salad, although the waitress told me that she hates Arugula and couldn't recommend it, I found it to be quite delicious with it's dried cranberries and jalapeno cucumber dressing (it was not a spicy dressing, just a little extra flavor). As for the beer, normal beer, cheaply priced. Good Stuff. We sat out on the patio and enjoyed the spring evening. My only complaint would be that they probably need one more server to help take care of the patio when the weather gets as nice as it has been. The service was a little slow, but nothing to keep me from coming back... again, and again, and again. Also, the patio is dog friendly, for well behaved dogs. :-)

This is a very good restaurant. The food was awesome. The burger BLT & C was awesome. The onion ring were very good. My wife got the homemade chips. They were fantastic. Her club sandwich was very good. These guys even had craft beer and it was not over priced. We will definitely be back here again. I even love the decorations all around the restaurant.  But I didn't see a Tennessee Volunteers flag  lol

Have been here 4 or 5 times and was happy each time. Service was great the employees there are enthusiastic and friendly. Portions are good, prices are good, and one if the more tastier places downtown. Will definitely be coming back.

This is probably a good restaurant. But to be honest every time I go there, my food is always cold. They need to heat it to the right temperature and by the way the restaurant was just open at that time. The only really good thing is the octopus if you are a seafood or spicy fan. But that's the only really good thing other than the ice cream. Please step up your game.

Pretty good food there. The service was great. There really are no jokes to be had, and nothing bad to say. Its a good place to go to brunch. The manager was a little awkward at the host stand, but once the real host returned we were seated without issue. Although they seated us (2) at a large table, and a few minutes later a large party came in and glared at us as they were escorted to a small table. That made things a bit more awkward. However, all in all the service and food were great. The eggs benedict was awesome good.

if you are meeting someone who is chronically late, establish this as your spot and kill time browsing through hootenany, a great little clothing store, or newbury comics, or even just to use the public bathroom and atm.  hosts some decent restaurants of the smaller chain variety (ben and jerry's, pho pasteur), and stacked outside newbury are all the local free entertainment mags one could ever desire.

Stopped in to look at refurbished Windows computers.  I was delighted with the help I got in selecting one (a Dell Latitude E5120); the sales person was interested in exactly what I wanted to do with the device and he helped me find one well within my price constraints (cheap).Service and product they sold me could not have been better.   Highly recommend this place.Keep it up.

I lived in Greece for a few months and this is the best Greek food I've tasted in the US! The ground up chick peas with pita given at every table is delicious. I had the falafel pita for lunch and the Greek ops fries are out of this world. Next time I'm in Orlando ill be back for dinner!

This was a good choice for a rainy day ramen craving.  Menu is simple.  Additional toppings are available.  Chashu was cooked perfectly... tender and flavorful.  It is a small place but those usually are the better ones.I ordered the miso deluxe bowl and it was perfect amount of ingredients.  It wasn't too salty, although we were told it was the saltier of the three options.Definitely going there again.

I'm actually kind of bummed that this place opened up and started taking a lot of great acts from some of the better venues in town, i.e. Paradise. I've been to two shows here so far. Yes, the acoustics and general cleanliness are better than the Avalon, but those were the only positive changes I saw. The security is way more uptight than they need to be. My friendly bouncer scrutinized my baggie of ibuprofen, tucked safely away in a side pocket. I had a friend who endured some embarrassment as her condoms were given the once-over. Is this necessary?Beer and coat check are overpriced, as many have noted. The larger stage and new decor do not make up for this. Bring my peeps back to the Paradise please!!
